title: Burn down defects and sweep design QA to a defensible GA bar
body:
## Context
R5 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9, sprints S23–S26, 2027-02-26 → 2027-03-25, version `1.1.0` GA) has four goals; this epic owns goal 3: *"Burn down accumulated defects, accepted risks and design-QA findings to a defensible level."* By the time R5 opens, twenty-two months of delivery (E01–E45) have produced a bug backlog that was triaged under the SLAs in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 but deliberately deferred where severity allowed ("P2 … may be scheduled next sprint with owner sign-off", "P3 … backlog, no release block"). In parallel, every net-new UI story shipped with a `design-qa` DoD clause (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2) whose discrepancies were allowed to be *"filed as a follow-up Bug"* rather than fixed in-story. Those two deferral valves are what this epic closes.

E49 is a **cross-area sweep**: it touches every module and every story domain rather than introducing new capability. Its four workstreams are (1) defect triage and burn-down, (2) a design-QA pass over every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` against the checklist in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12, (3) an empty/loading/error state and copy audit centred on the shared state patterns SCR-150…SCR-159, and (4) a hotkey conflict audit plus the accepted-risk re-review with expiry enforcement demanded by `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` §1.3 and roadmap exit criterion 9.3.4.

E49 is the last epic to close before GA (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12.6: `R5 → GA | e49 [S23-S26], e48 [S25-S26] | 2027-03-25`), and the roadmap dependency graph records `E47 --> E49` and `E43 --> E49`: accessibility findings (E47) and pen-test remediation leftovers (E43) both flow into this burn-down queue.

References: `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6 (Bug DoR/DoD), `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11, `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12–§13, `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` §1.3, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Triage & measurement**: a single defect queue with enforced severity/SLA fields, saved board queries, a weekly triage ritual, and a burn-down/ageing dashboard so "defensible level" is a number, not an opinion (E49-T01, E49-T02).
- **Root-cause clustering spike** over the accumulated backlog so fixes attack themes, not symptoms (E49-K01).
- **Three burn-down waves**: P0/P1 to zero (E49-S01, E49-S02) and P2 down to ≤10 with owners and target sprints (E49-S03), matching roadmap exit criterion 9.3.3.
- **Design-QA remediation** of token/spacing/type/state discrepancies across the screens catalogue (E49-S04), driven by the audit protocol and findings ledger from E49-D01.
- **State-pattern remediation**: every empty / loading / error / disconnected / degraded / 403 / 404 / crash / rate-limited surface conforms to SCR-150…SCR-159 and CMP-014, CMP-015, CMP-026, CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-029, CMP-089, CMP-090, CMP-091, CMP-092 (E49-S05, design in E49-D02).
- **Copy review** across all user-visible strings incl. error registry messages (E49-S06, design/content spec in E49-D03).
- **Hotkey conflict audit** across every context in SCR-013 and SCR-113 satisfying US-SET-002's conflict-detection and reserved-key scenarios, plus a CI lint that keeps the keymap conflict-free (E49-S07, E49-T04).
- **Accepted-risk re-review with expiry enforcement** over `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` (E49-T03).
- **Doc reconciliation + ADR** recording the GA defect-disposition policy (E49-T05).
- **Design track**: E49-D01…E49-D05 (audit protocol, state-pattern spec, copy/terminology spec, motion sweep, final design sign-off).
- **QA track**: E49-Q01…E49-Q04 (GA regression pack, exploratory charters/bug bash, state-matrix black-box plan, a11y + QA sign-off).
- **Security track**: E49-X01, E49-X02 (STRIDE of the fix/hotfix path, security regression verification of every fix).

## Out of scope
- New product capability of any kind. A defect whose fix requires new capability is re-filed as a post-GA Story, not absorbed here.
- Performance optimisation work — owned by **E46**; E49 only files and verifies perf *defects* against E46's budgets.
- Accessibility remediation of the WCAG audit itself — owned by **E47**; E49 verifies that E47's fixes did not regress and absorbs only the residual, non-a11y design-QA findings.
- Documentation authoring, runbooks and the GA checklist — owned by **E48**.
- Pen-test finding remediation — owned by **E43**; residual low-severity findings that E43 deferred enter this queue as normal bugs.
- Android and any separate admin application (owner decision 2026-09-14; admin screens are RBAC-gated screens inside the web app).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The GA defect bar is met
  Given the GA candidate build at the end of S26
  When the defect queue is reported
  Then there are zero open P0 and zero open P1 bugs against shipped scope
  And open P2 bugs number at most 10, each with a named owner and a target post-GA sprint
  And every open P3 has been triaged with a recorded disposition

Scenario: Design QA is closed out per screen
  Given the design-QA findings ledger produced by E49-D01
  When the ledger is reviewed at the S25 design sign-off
  Then every screen in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md has a recorded verdict of pass or accepted-exception
  And every accepted exception names an owner, a reason and a post-GA ticket

Scenario: Accepted risks are re-decided, not extended
  Given docs/plan/32-risk-register.md contains risks with Status "Accepted"
  When the R5 expiry enforcement pass runs
  Then every accepted risk has a current owner, an expiry date and a dated review record
  And any acceptance whose expiry has passed has been explicitly re-decided (re-accepted with a new expiry, mitigated, or escalated), never silently carried

Scenario: A regression sneaks in during burn-down
  Given a fix merged in a burn-down wave breaks an unrelated area
  When the GA regression pack (E49-Q01) runs nightly
  Then the failure is detected within one nightly cycle
  And the regression is filed at the severity of the broken area, blocking the wave's closure until fixed

Scenario: No bug closes without a guard
  Given a bug ticket in this epic is moved to Done
  When its Definition of Done is checked
  Then a regression test exists at the appropriate pyramid layer that fails on the pre-fix commit and passes after
  Or the bug is a pure documentation/cosmetic P3 with that exemption stated explicitly on the ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Queue model.** One GitHub Project view backed by the existing schema (`Kind=Bug`, `Priority`, `Component`, `Perspective`, `Risk`, `Sprint`). No new tracker. Severity mapping is exactly `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 (P0 2 h triage / P1 1 business day / P2 3 business days / P3 1 sprint).
- **Wave cadence.** S23 = triage + clustering + wave 1; S24 = wave 2 + design-QA remediation + copy; S25 = P2 sweep + state remediation + design sign-off; S26 = verification, GA regression, sign-offs. Fix PRs stay ≤400 LOC per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; each wave is a series of small PRs, never a mega-PR.
- **Themes over symptoms.** E49-K01 clusters the backlog by root-cause family (state-machine races, token drift, missing empty/error states, formatting/locale, keymap, WS reconnect edge cases, RBAC copy leakage). A cluster with ≥3 members must be fixed at its shared root, with a single guard test covering the family.
- **Freeze discipline.** From the start of S26 week 2 the GA candidate is under change freeze: only P0/P1 fixes merge, each requiring the hotfix review path in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §8.
- **Definition of "defensible".** Codified in the ADR from E49-T05: zero P0/P1; ≤10 P2 with owners; all P3 triaged; every accepted risk in-date; every design-QA finding pass-or-accepted; regression guard per closed bug.

## Test plan
- **Regression pack (E49-Q01)**: consolidated Playwright web + Electron suite covering the primary trading flow, admin surfaces, replay and the state matrix; runs nightly across S23–S26 and on every burn-down PR's merge queue entry.
- **Exploratory charters (E49-Q02)**: 60–120 min charters per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 for OMS/order path, rule engine, fan-out, chart-engine visual correctness at extreme density, admin/RBAC probing; plus two cross-team bug bashes.
- **State matrix (E49-Q04)**: black-box plan asserting every panel's empty / loading / error / disconnected / degraded / permission-denied / rate-limited rendering against SCR-150…SCR-159.
- **A11y (E49-Q03)**: axe-core, pa11y-ci catalogue sweep and a manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass over the GA candidate, confirming E47's remediation held.
- **Security (E49-X02)**: SAST/SCA/secrets/DAST sweep on the GA candidate; targeted re-test of every fix touching auth, RBAC, keys, OMS or fan-out.
- Coverage gates unchanged: ≥85% backend/engine, ≥80% frontend; a burn-down PR may not regress its package baseline.

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` relevant to a burn-down epic are process threats rather than feature threats: a rushed fix bypassing review (tampering), a hotfix path used to ship unreviewed code (elevation of privilege), a "cosmetic" copy change leaking existence of admin objects in a 403/404 (information disclosure — SCR-154/SCR-155 explicitly require identical 404 copy for admin routes), and a regression re-opening a closed pen-test finding (repudiation of the E43 sign-off). E49-X01 models these with STRIDE; E49-X02 verifies them on the candidate. Data classification: fixes may touch secrets (`api_keys`), financial state (OMS tables) and PII (users) — any such fix carries the `security` label and a Security-engineer review per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Accessibility notes
Every UI fix in this epic re-enters the a11y gate: axe-core green on the touched screen, keyboard-only path verified, focus order and visible focus checked against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Copy fixes must preserve accessible names and live-region semantics (a shorter string is not automatically a better accessible name). The state-pattern work is a11y-load-bearing: SCR-151 forbids a bare "No data", SCR-152 mandates a single `role="alert"` then a persistent banner, SCR-153 mandates `role="status"` naming the degraded capability.

## Performance notes
E49 must not regress E46's budgets: the CI-enforced budget checks from E46 (frame budget, WS→pixel latency, startup and workspace-restore time) are required checks on every burn-down PR, and a >5% regression on any hard budget fails the build per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4. Fixes to hot paths (chart engine, book application, fan-out serialisation) additionally record a before/after benchmark on the ticket.

## Observability
- Metrics: `defects_open{severity}`, `defects_opened_total`, `defects_closed_total`, `defect_age_days` histogram, `sla_breach_total{severity}` exported from the triage tooling into the existing Prometheus/Grafana stack.
- A GA-readiness Grafana panel showing the burn-down curve against the S26 target line.
- Audit: risk-register re-review decisions are recorded as dated entries in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`; hotkey rebinding of trading actions remains audited as `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`.
- Analytics already emitted by the state screens (`empty_state_shown`, `error.403_shown`, `error.404_shown`, `app.error_boundary_triggered`, `degraded.entered`, `ratelimit.hit`) is used as the *input* to the state audit: surfaces users hit often and should not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded Won't/Later disposition.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1; ≤10 open P2 with owners and target sprints; all P3 triaged.
- [ ] Design-QA ledger closed: every screen pass-or-accepted; CDO/design sign-off recorded (E49-D05).
- [ ] Every accepted risk in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` in-date with a dated review record.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core + pa11y-ci clean on the GA candidate; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] perf: no E46 budget regression on the GA candidate; 72 h soak unaffected by burn-down merges.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, GA scan sweep clean or accepted, Security-engineer sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off: GA regression pack green, charter notes attached, epic-level exploratory pass recorded.
- [ ] Docs: plan docs reconciled with shipped behaviour; ADR for the GA defect-disposition policy merged.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at the final Sprint Review with the burn-down curve and the design-QA ledger shown.
- [ ] Retro note filed with process learnings as Chore tickets.

## Dependencies
- **E47 Accessibility conformance** (roadmap edge `E47 --> E49`): a11y findings that E47 cannot close in S23–S25 arrive here as bugs; E49's verification pass confirms E47's fixes.
- **E43 Security hardening & pen-test remediation** (roadmap edge `E43 --> E49`): residual low-severity pen-test findings enter this queue.

**Non-blocking scope inputs (not `blocked_by`).** The roadmap dependency graph (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §13) encodes exactly two direct predecessors of E49 — `E47 --> E49` and `E43 --> E49` — so only those two appear in `blocked_by`. The epics below supply scope and gates to E49 but are *not* direct graph predecessors; they are reached transitively (E42 → E43, E44 → E47, E44 → E46 → E48) and E49 can start without them being complete:
- **E46 Performance hardening** (transitive via `E44 --> E46`): E46's CI-enforced budgets are the gate every burn-down PR must pass once they land; until then the pre-existing budget checks apply.
- **E44 Live-enablement gating** (transitive via `E44 --> E47 --> E49`): live-mode surfaces are included in the design-QA and state sweeps as they become available.
- **E42 Admin screens** (transitive via `E42 --> E43 --> E49`): admin surfaces (SCR-120…SCR-149) are in the sweep scope.
- **E48 Documentation, runbooks & GA readiness**: consumes E49's ledger and ADR for the GA checklist.

## Branch
`feat/defect-burndown-<short>` per child; fixes use `fix/<area>-<short>` per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`. PR size: ≤400 LOC diff; one root-cause cluster per PR; never batch unrelated fixes.

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9 (R5), §10.1 Gantt `E49 Defect & design-QA [S23-S26]`, §12.6 gate table, §13 dependency graph.
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 (black-box QA process, bug taxonomy, white-box checklist), §12 (a11y protocol).
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 (design QA checklist), §13 (design-ahead & sign-off).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-150…SCR-159 (shared state patterns), SCR-013/SCR-113 (hotkeys).
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` §1.3 (review cadence, accepted-risk expiry).
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6 (Bug), §8 (cross-kind gating).

## Children — dependency graph

## Agent guidance

Multiple agents will work E49's children in parallel. To pick the next ticket:

1. Respect `blocked_by` on each child ticket — do not start a ticket whose blockers are not yet Done.
2. Prefer the epic's own dependency graph (see `## Child dependency graph` / `## Children — dependency graph` section above) over guessing from titles.
3. Design (`-D0x`) and Spike (`-K0x`) tickets generally gate their dependent Story/Task tickets — pick those first if unblocked.
4. QA (`-Q0x`) and Security (`-X0x`) tickets are epic-closing; they depend on most Task/Story work and should be picked last.
5. Two agents must not take tickets that both modify the same non-generated file; check open PRs/branches for path overlap before starting.
6. Shared interfaces to agree before parallel work starts: any WS/REST contract change, any shared machine.json under `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/machines/`, and any shared design-system token — post in the ticket comments before changing.

title: Author the design-QA audit protocol and open the per-screen findings ledger
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 defines the design-QA checklist that every component and screen ticket must pass before Done, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI stories — but explicitly permits discrepancies to be *"filed as follow-up Bug"* rather than fixed in-story. Twenty-two months of that valve leaves a backlog of unverified screens and deferred findings. R5 exit criterion 3 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 requires that backlog to reach a defensible level before GA.

This ticket produces the *instrument*: a repeatable audit protocol plus a ledger with one row per screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, so that E49-S04 (remediation) has an ordered, evidence-backed work queue rather than a vibe. It lands in S22 — two sprints ahead of the S24 remediation story — satisfying the design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` and `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §13.

The roadmap notes (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5, "After D-S18 the design org shifts to design-QA and defect support") that design capacity in R5 is reserved precisely for this.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Audit protocol document** `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-design-qa-protocol.md`: how one screen is audited, in what order, with what evidence, by whom, and what constitutes pass / finding / accepted-exception. Derived verbatim from the four checklist groups in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 — Tokens & visual, Behaviour & states, Accessibility, Trading-specific safety, Consistency.
- **Per-screen ledger** `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-design-qa-ledger.csv` with one row per `SCR-nnn` in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (SCR-001 … SCR-159, including the admin band SCR-120…SCR-149 and the shared state band SCR-150…SCR-159), columns: screen id, screen name, owning epic, auditor, audit date, verdict (pass / findings / accepted-exception / not-applicable), finding count by severity, linked bug keys, notes.
- **Severity mapping** from design-QA finding → bug priority using `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 (token drift that changes a trading signal's meaning = P1; wrong-but-readable spacing = P3; missing designed empty/error state = P2; a11y AA violation = P2 minimum).
- **Evidence standard**: each audited screen captures a Figma-vs-build side-by-side in all three themes (dark, light, high-contrast) at both density modes (compact, comfortable), per §12's "verified in all three themes … at both density modes" clause.
- **Sampling rule for high-variance surfaces**: chart surfaces (SCR-030…SCR-054) are audited at three data densities (sparse, typical, extreme footprint density) because their visual state is data-dependent.
- **Prioritised audit order** so that trading-critical surfaces (SCR-030 chart workspace, SCR-050/051 DOM ladder & heatmap, SCR-060 order ticket, SCR-070 positions grid, SCR-074 env switch) are audited first.
- **Pilot audit of 10 screens** executed inside this ticket to prove the protocol produces actionable, non-duplicative findings before the full sweep is commissioned.
- **Design-system contribution**: any near-duplicate component discovered during the pilot is raised against `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` as a consolidation note rather than silently tolerated (§12 "Reuses an existing CMP-* rather than introducing a near-duplicate").

## Out of scope
- Fixing anything — remediation is E49-S04 / E49-S05 / E49-S06.
- The WCAG audit itself, owned by **E47**; this ledger *records* E47's verdict per screen rather than re-deriving it.
- New screen or component design. No new `SCR-` or `CMP-` ids are created by this epic.
- Performance findings — routed to **E46**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ledger covers the catalogue exactly
  Given docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the ledger is generated
  Then it contains exactly one row per SCR id in the catalogue
  And any id present in the catalogue but absent from the ledger fails the ledger's own self-check script

Scenario: A finding is actionable without a conversation
  Given a designer audits SCR-060 and records a finding
  When an engineer opens the resulting bug
  Then the bug names the checklist clause breached, the token or state involved, the expected value from the Figma spec, the observed value in the build, the theme and density it reproduces in, and a screenshot pair

Scenario: The pilot proves the protocol
  Given the 10 pilot screens are audited
  When the findings are reviewed with the design-system lead and an engineer
  Then at least 80 percent of findings are accepted as actionable without clarification
  And any protocol step that produced ambiguous findings is revised before the full sweep is commissioned

Scenario: An accepted exception is never silent
  Given a discrepancy is deliberately not going to be fixed before GA
  When it is recorded in the ledger
  Then the row carries verdict "accepted-exception" with a named owner, a written reason and a post-GA follow-up ticket key
  And a row with verdict "accepted-exception" and no follow-up key fails the self-check

Scenario: Theme and density coverage is enforced
  Given a screen is marked audited
  When the evidence attached is inspected
  Then side-by-side captures exist for dark, light and high-contrast at both compact and comfortable density
  Or an explicit not-applicable reason is written per missing combination
```

## Technical notes / design
- The ledger is a CSV under version control (not a Figma comment thread) so the self-check script can be run in CI and so the GA evidence pack in **E48** can cite a commit hash.
- Self-check script `scripts/design_qa_ledger_check.py`: parses `### SCR-` headings from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, diffs against ledger ids, validates verdict enum, validates that `accepted-exception` rows carry owner + reason + follow-up key, and that `findings` rows carry at least one bug key. Exit non-zero on violation; wired into the `docs` CI job.
- Audit ordering uses the traceability matrix `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` to weight screens by the number of Must stories they serve.
- Figma structure and naming follow `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §10; token references are Tier-2/Tier-3 names only, never hex, so a finding is expressed as "uses `color.surface.raised` where the spec says `color.surface.sunken`".
- Effort model: budget ~15 minutes per simple state screen, ~45 minutes per dense trading screen; the pilot calibrates these numbers and the calibrated figures size E49-S04.

## Test plan
- Unit: `scripts/design_qa_ledger_check.py` tested against fixture ledgers — complete, missing-row, bad-verdict, exception-without-owner, findings-without-bug-key.
- Process validation: the 10-screen pilot is the test of the protocol; acceptance is the ≥80% actionable rate above.
- Contract / integration / e2e / perf / chaos: N/A — this is a process and document deliverable.
- Fixtures: a 5-row synthetic ledger and a trimmed screens-catalogue fixture under `tests/fixtures/design_qa/`.
- Coverage target: ≥85% on the new script (it lives in the backend/tooling package).

## Security notes
The ledger and its screenshots may capture live-looking trading data. Evidence captures must use the demo environment and fixture symbols only — never a live account, never a real API key fragment, never a real balance. This is an information-disclosure control from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; the protocol states it as a hard rule and the pilot verifies it. Data classification of the ledger itself: internal, no secrets. No `security` review label required beyond this note.

## Accessibility notes
The protocol's Accessibility group is copied from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 and cross-checks `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: keyboard-interaction table completed and matching a tested path; accessible-name/role table completed; for any canvas/WebGL-adjacent surface the DOM-mirror / windowed-tree / non-spatial-alternative strategy is specified per §6 and not deferred; motion-safe/motion-reduce pair specified; 24px compact / 40–44px comfortable hit targets. Findings in this group are P2 minimum.

## Performance notes
Auditing must not be performed against a build running under a profiler or with degraded rendering, or spacing and text metrics will be misread. The protocol requires the reference machine and the `balanced` performance profile from SCR-118, with SCR-046 diagnostics confirming the engine is not in `degraded-2d` during capture.

## Observability
No runtime telemetry added. The ledger's counts feed the burn-down dashboard (E49-T02) as a separate series `design_qa_findings_open{severity}` so design debt is visible next to functional defects.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Protocol document merged and reviewed by the design-system lead and one engineer.
- [ ] Ledger committed with one row per catalogue screen; self-check script green in CI.
- [ ] 10-screen pilot executed, findings filed, ≥80% actionable rate recorded.
- [ ] Calibrated per-screen effort figures published and used to size E49-S04.
- [ ] Severity mapping agreed with QA and recorded in the protocol.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 cross-links the protocol.
- [ ] Design sign-off from the CDO or delegate recorded on the ticket per `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §13.3.
- [ ] Demo: pilot findings walked through at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with required approvals.

## Dependencies
- **E47** must have published its per-screen WCAG verdicts (or their in-progress state) so the ledger references rather than duplicates them.
- **E44** and **E42** define the live-gating and admin surfaces that must appear in the ledger. These are *scope inputs, not blockers* — neither is a direct predecessor of E49 in the roadmap dependency graph (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §13), so the ledger is authored against the screens catalogue and rows for those surfaces are filled in as the screens land.

## Branch

title: Specify the unified empty, loading and error state patterns for the GA sweep
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` defines nine shared state patterns — SCR-150 global boot, SCR-151 empty state, SCR-152 disconnected/reconnecting, SCR-153 degraded mode, SCR-154 permission denied, SCR-155 not found, SCR-156 error boundary, SCR-157 version mismatch, SCR-158 rate-limited, SCR-159 offline/shell — each with a design sign-off checklist. They were specified once, early, then instantiated independently by fifteen epics across twenty-two months. Drift is certain: some panels will show a bare spinner where SCR-150 forbids one, some will show "No data" where SCR-151 forbids it, some will disable trading without saying why where SCR-152 requires the reason.

R5 goal 3 includes an explicit "empty/loading/error state audit". This ticket is the design half: the single, normative spec against which E49-S05 remediates and E49-Q04 tests. It lands in S22, two sprints before the S24/S25 remediation, per the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Normative state spec** in Figma plus a written companion, covering the full anatomy of each pattern and the *exact* component composition it must use:
  - SCR-150 boot: staged progress with named stages, 5 s slow-boot message, 15 s cancel/reload, per-stage failure with an action — CMP-014 Spinner/Loader, CMP-015 Skeleton, CMP-038 InlineSpinnerText, CMP-207 BuildFooter.
  - SCR-151 empty: heading stating the fact, one sentence of cause, one primary action, one secondary learn-more, recorder-dependent variant carrying the recording-start timestamp; three classes (nothing created yet / nothing matches the filter / data not recorded yet); role-aware action-vs-explanation variants — CMP-001, CMP-019, CMP-021, CMP-026 EmptyState.
  - SCR-152 disconnected: global banner + per-panel stale shading, last-good timestamp per panel, trading visibly blocked with the reason, the "native stops still protect your positions" reassurance where true — CMP-028, CMP-035, CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay, CMP-078 StaleDataShade.
  - SCR-153 degraded: per-cause variants, what still works vs what does not, disclosed feature-shedding, manual reduce-quality control, exit/restore — CMP-028, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
  - SCR-154 403: names resource and missing permission without disclosing existence of admin-only objects, "ask the owner" route, link back, correlation id — CMP-079 RbacGate, CMP-089 ForbiddenState.
  - SCR-155 404: attempted route echoed, likely destinations, deleted-object vs unknown-route copy, admin routes 404 identically for non-owners — CMP-090 NotFoundState.
  - SCR-156 crash: panel-level and route-level variants, surviving surrounding UI, correlation id + copy-diagnostics, repeated-crash stop state — CMP-033 CopyButton, CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock, CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback.
  - SCR-157 version mismatch: blocking vs non-blocking variants, what stops working, per-shell update action, do-not-update-mid-trade guidance with open-position count — CMP-096 WhatsNewPanel, CMP-207.
  - SCR-158 rate-limited: per-scope variants (exchange per-UID, backend per-user, fan-out budget), countdown, held-action queue with explicit replay confirmation, link to SCR-147 — CMP-023, CMP-028, CMP-035, CMP-069.
  - SCR-159 offline/shell: offline vs tailnet-unreachable vs backend-unreachable with distinct accurate copy, GPU-unavailable fallback and its limitations, browser-vs-Electron differences — CMP-092, CMP-207, CMP-215 FloatingWindowFrame.
- **Loading-state decision table**: when a surface uses a skeleton (CMP-015/CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart) versus an inline spinner (CMP-038) versus a progress bar (CMP-023), keyed on expected duration and whether the layout is known in advance.
- **A conformance rubric** — a short per-surface checklist an engineer can self-apply before requesting design QA.
- **Design-system contribution**: propose the missing variants discovered while writing the spec back into `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` as variant additions to existing CMP ids, never new ids.

## Out of scope
- Implementing or fixing any surface (E49-S05).
- Copy authoring — the words themselves are E49-D03; this ticket specifies the *slots* the words go in.
- New state patterns. SCR-150…SCR-159 are the closed set.
- Motion specification, which is E49-D04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every pattern has every state drawn
  Given the nine shared state patterns
  When the Figma file is reviewed for sign-off
  Then each pattern has a frame per documented variant in its catalogue entry
  And each frame exists in dark, light and high-contrast themes at both density modes

Scenario: An engineer can self-check without asking a designer
  Given an engineer has a panel that can be empty
  When they apply the conformance rubric
  Then they can determine which of the three empty classes applies, which components to compose, and what the accessible name must be, without further clarification

Scenario: The 403 pattern does not leak existence
  Given a non-owner requests an admin-only route
  When the 403 and 404 specs are compared
  Then the specification requires identical copy to any other 404 for admin routes
  And the 403 variant names the missing permission only for resources the actor is permitted to know exist

Scenario: Loading choice is deterministic
  Given a surface with an unknown load duration and a known layout
  When the loading-state decision table is applied
  Then exactly one treatment is selected, and the table has no cell that permits two answers

Scenario: The spec forbids the known anti-patterns
  When the spec is reviewed
  Then it explicitly forbids a bare spinner with no staged description, a bare "No data" string, an icon-only empty state, and a disabled control without the disabled-with-reason pattern CMP-079
```

## Technical notes / design
- Composition is expressed as component recipes (ordered CMP ids with their variant props), so E49-S05 can be executed as mechanical conformance rather than re-design.
- Accessible-name templates are part of the spec, not an afterthought: e.g. SCR-153's per-panel badge accessible name is "`<panel>`: `<capability>` degraded — `<what still works>`".
- The spec states which analytics event each state must emit (`empty_state_shown{surface,reason}`, `error.403_shown`, `error.404_shown`, `app.error_boundary_triggered{component,correlationId,stackHash}`, `degraded.entered{cause,sheddedFeatures}`, `ratelimit.hit{scope,endpointClass,retryAfterMs}`) so the audit can be driven from telemetry as well as by inspection.
- Empty states must render without initialising heavy resources (no GL context, no subscriptions) per SCR-151's performance clause; the spec calls this out so remediation does not accidentally mount an engine to show "nothing here yet".

## Test plan
- Design review: spec walked through against each catalogue entry's own "Design sign-off acceptance checklist"; every checkbox in those nine checklists must map to a frame or an explicit N/A.
- The rubric is dry-run by two engineers on two unrelated panels; disagreement between them on any rubric answer is a defect in the rubric.
- Storybook: the spec enumerates the exact story matrix E49-S05 must produce, so QA can assert story existence mechanically.
- Unit/contract/integration/perf/chaos: N/A for this ticket.

## Security notes
The 403/404 specification is a security control, not cosmetics: SCR-155 requires that admin routes 404 for non-owners with copy identical to any other 404, so the admin area's existence is not disclosed. SCR-154 requires that the resource and permission are named *without* leaking whether an admin-only resource exists. Both are information-disclosure mitigations from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; the spec is reviewed by the Security engineer for this clause specifically. Correlation ids shown to users must be opaque and must not encode account or user identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
Per-pattern requirements are normative and taken from the catalogue: SCR-150 announces progress politely at each phase and never uses a bare spinner; SCR-151 always has a heading plus a causal sentence plus either an action or an explicit statement that no action is available to this role; SCR-152 fires `role="alert"` once then persists as a banner and does not announce the countdown on every tick; SCR-153 uses `role="status"` naming the degraded capability in plain sentences; SCR-156 uses a `role="alert"` region with the stack trace behind an expandable labelled as technical detail; SCR-158 announces countdowns at most once per 10 s. The spec carries the accessible-name template for each.

## Performance notes
SCR-151: empty surfaces cost nothing — no GL context, no subscriptions. SCR-154: the 403 renders from the server response with no additional fetches in ≤200 ms. SCR-155: client-side resolution, no network call. SCR-150: cold start to interactive shell ≤2.5 s on the reference machine with staged progress. These budgets are restated in the spec so remediation is measured against them.

## Observability
The spec fixes the analytics contract for every state surface (event name and payload shape listed above), which is what makes the telemetry-driven half of the E49-S05 audit possible: surfaces with a high `empty_state_shown` rate and no user action are flagged as product defects, not just visual ones.

- [ ] Figma frames complete for all nine patterns across themes and densities.

- [ ] Conformance rubric dry-run by two engineers with no disagreements outstanding.

title: Write the GA copy and terminology specification for every user-visible string
body:
## Context
R5 goal 3 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 lists a **copy review** as part of E49. Copy in this product is not decoration: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` repeatedly makes wording a functional requirement — SCR-152 must say "Trading is disabled while offline" *and* "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected"; SCR-153 must state per cause what still works and what does not; SCR-154 must never be a bare "Forbidden"; heuristic detectors must be labelled *estimated* (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge) because `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` classifies iceberg/stop-run detection as estimated and the risk register carries an advice-boundary concern. Fifteen epics wrote that copy independently.

This ticket produces the normative terminology and copy spec that E49-S06 applies. It lands in S22, two sprints ahead of the S24 remediation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Terminology lexicon**: the single approved term for each concept, with banned synonyms — e.g. *trade group* (not "basket"/"batch"), *fan-out*, *native stop-loss* (not "exchange stop"), *Demo* / *Live* (never "testnet"/"paper" in UI chrome; "paper trading" only where US-PAPER stories use it), *arm/disarm*, *kill-switch*, *flatten*, *reduce-only*, *estimated* for every heuristic output, *recorded history* vs *replay*, *workspace* vs *layout*, *rule* vs *alert*, *Owner/Manager/Viewer* for RBAC roles exactly as `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` names them.
- **Voice and tense rules**: second person, present tense, active voice; state the fact first, then the cause, then the action (matching SCR-151's mandated anatomy); no blame ("you entered an invalid value" → "this value must be between X and Y"); no exclamation marks; no jargon without an InfoPanel link.
- **Error-message standard** applied across the REST/WS error registry referenced by `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`: every user-facing error states what happened, why, what to do next, and carries a correlation id; codes are never shown alone.
- **Safety-copy rules** for destructive and trading actions (US-SET-003 policy surfaces, SCR-015, SCR-029, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-129): confirm dialogs name the exact quantity, symbol, account count and environment; hold-to-confirm states its duration; Live copy is never softer than Demo copy.
- **Estimated/heuristic disclosure rules**: every detector output (iceberg, stop-run, regime, imbalance) carries CMP-227 and links to its methodology InfoPanel; the words "detected", "confirmed" and "signal" are banned for estimated outputs in favour of "estimated".
- **Numbers, units, time**: applies US-SET-006 — display honours the user's zone and separators, exports are always ISO-8601 with an explicit offset, the zone is labelled wherever a timestamp appears.
- **String inventory**: an extracted list of every user-visible string in the web app (i18n-style extraction even though the app ships English-only) written to `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-string-inventory.csv` with screen, component, current text, verdict, proposed text.
- **Light UX research**: a 60-minute read-aloud session with the Owner over the twelve most safety-critical strings (order confirms, kill-switch, flatten, live switch, disconnected banner) to check they are understood under time pressure; 5–8 findings written up.

## Out of scope
- Localisation or any i18n runtime. The extraction is an audit instrument, not a translation pipeline.
- Changing product behaviour to match nicer copy — if the copy is right and the behaviour is wrong, that is a bug for the owning epic, not a copy edit.
- Marketing or documentation prose — **E48** owns the user guide.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One term per concept
  Given the terminology lexicon
  When the string inventory is scanned for banned synonyms
  Then every occurrence is listed with its screen and a proposed replacement
  And the lexicon has no concept with two approved terms

Scenario: Every error message is complete
  Given a user-facing error string in the inventory
  When it is graded against the error-message standard
  Then it states what happened, why, and what to do next, and a correlation id is available
  Or it is recorded as a finding with a proposed rewrite

Scenario: Estimated outputs are never asserted as fact
  Given a detector output string
  When it is graded
  Then it uses "estimated" and is accompanied by CMP-227 plus a methodology link
  And any use of "detected" or "confirmed" for a heuristic output is a P2 finding

Scenario: Live copy is never softer than Demo
  Given a destructive-action confirm string that differs between environments
  When both variants are compared
  Then the Live variant is at least as explicit about consequence as the Demo variant
  And any counter-example is filed as a P1 finding

Scenario: The read-aloud session finds real problems
  Given the twelve safety-critical strings
  When the Owner reads each aloud and states what they believe will happen
  Then any string where the stated expectation differs from actual behaviour is a P1 finding regardless of how well-written it reads
```

## Technical notes / design
- Extraction: a script walks the React source for JSX text nodes, `aria-label`, `title`, `placeholder`, toast/dialog builders and the error-registry map, emitting the CSV. It is deliberately over-inclusive; triage prunes.
- Accessible names are in scope as strings: an `aria-label` is user-visible to a screen-reader user and is graded by the same standard.
- Grading is by exception — most strings pass; the deliverable is the finding list plus the lexicon, not a rewritten inventory.
- Copy that is load-bearing for safety (confirms, disconnected banner, live switch) is marked `frozen` in the lexicon: changing it post-GA requires design + security review, not a drive-by edit.

## Test plan
- Unit: the extraction script tested against a fixture component tree (nested JSX, aria-label, template literal, dynamic string) asserting expected extraction and expected known-limitation misses.
- Lint rule proposal: a banned-synonym ESLint rule fed by the lexicon, delivered as a proposal here and implemented in E49-S06.
- Manual: the read-aloud session with the Owner, documented.
- Coverage: ≥80% on the frontend tooling script.

## Security notes
Copy is an information-disclosure surface. The spec forbids: echoing raw exception text or stack traces into user-facing strings (SCR-156 puts technical detail behind an expandable, not in the headline); including account identifiers, key fragments or internal hostnames in errors; and any 403/404 wording that reveals whether an admin-only resource exists (see `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-154/SCR-155). Correlation ids must be opaque. Reviewed by the Security engineer.

## Accessibility notes
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` makes accessible names part of conformance. The spec requires: names that make sense out of context ("Cancel order 12 BTCUSDT" not "Cancel"); no reliance on visual position ("the button below"); live-region text that is announceable and short enough to be useful at the configured verbosity (US-SET-007 verbosity levels); and never using colour words as the sole carrier of meaning ("buy side" not "the green side").

## Performance notes
N/A — no runtime impact. The extraction script runs offline and is not part of the app bundle.

## Observability
Strings that appear in analytics payloads (`empty_state_shown{reason}`, `degraded.entered{cause}`) are enumerated so a copy change does not silently break a dashboard query; any renamed reason/cause value is listed for the dashboard owner.

title: Sweep motion and reduced-motion behaviour across every animated surface
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §2.6 and §7 define the motion token set and the rule that every animated property ships a motion-safe / motion-reduce pair; §12's design-QA checklist requires that pair to be specified. US-SET-007 makes it a product requirement: with reduced motion enabled by preference or OS setting, "heatmap fades, panel transitions and chart inertia are disabled or replaced with instant changes". Across twenty-two months, animations were added per-epic — heatmap trails, bubble entry, toast slide-ins, panel docking, replay scrubbing, node-editor edge routing, alert flashes — and no single pass has ever verified the reduced-motion half of each pair actually exists.

- **Normative reduced-motion mapping**: for each motion class, what "reduced" means precisely — removed, replaced with an instant state change, or replaced with a cross-fade under 100 ms — rather than a blanket "turn it off", which would break affordances such as the SCR-152 reconnect countdown.
- **Token conformance list**: every animation must use §2.6 duration/easing tokens; hardcoded values are findings.
- **Trading-safety motion rules**: motion must never delay the readability of an order, position or price value; a hold-to-confirm progress indicator is exempt from reduction because it communicates a required duration (US-SET-003 mandates a visible progress indicator), and the spec records that exemption explicitly as an essential-motion exception.

- Implementing the fixes (E49-S04).

```gherkin
  Given the hold-to-confirm progress indicator
```

N/A — motion carries no threat surface. One note: the instrumentation hook is dev-build only and must not ship in the production bundle; its absence from the production build is asserted by a bundle check.

This ticket is primarily an accessibility deliverable. title: Spike: cluster the accumulated defect backlog by root cause to plan the waves
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2 requires that a bug's *root cause* be fixed, not its symptom. Applied one bug at a time across a backlog accumulated over twenty-two months, that produces dozens of near-identical local fixes and misses the shared defect that generated them. The epic's plan (see E49's Technical notes) is explicitly themes-over-symptoms: a cluster with three or more members is fixed at its shared root with one guard test covering the family.

This spike answers: **what are the actual clusters, how large is each, and which are worth a root fix versus individual patches?** Its output orders the three burn-down waves (E49-S01/S02/S03) and sizes them honestly. Timebox: 4 working days, agreed with the Architect, per §5.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Question 1**: What root-cause families exist in the open backlog, and what fraction of open defects does each explain?
- **Question 2**: For each family with ≥3 members, is a single root fix cheaper and safer than N local fixes, given the ≤400 LOC PR rule and the R5 change-freeze schedule?
- **Question 3**: Which families are *test-gap* families — defects that a missing test layer would have caught — so the guard test can be added once at the right layer rather than N times?
- **Deliverables**: a clustering report `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-root-cause-clusters.md`; `cluster/<name>` labels applied across the backlog; a per-cluster recommendation (root-fix / patch individually / accept / re-file as post-GA Story) with rough sizing; and the ordered wave plan handed to E49-S01/S02/S03.
- **Hypothesised starting taxonomy** (to be confirmed or refuted, not assumed): state-machine and race conditions in OMS/rule runtime; WS reconnect and gap-fill edge cases; design-token drift; missing or ad-hoc empty/loading/error states; number/time/locale formatting inconsistencies; keymap conflicts and context leakage; RBAC copy and disclosure leakage in 403/404 paths; chart-engine correctness at extreme zoom/density; fixture/determinism problems in replay; Electron-vs-browser shell divergence.
- **ADR**: `docs/plan/27-adrs/` entry recording the decision on which families get a root fix, including the "defer, need more data" outcome for any family the timebox could not resolve — per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 an ADR is required even for a deferral.

## Out of scope
- Fixing anything. Explicitly **not** expected to produce production-shippable code; any prototype is throwaway and its branch is left unmerged.
- Re-triaging severities (E49-T01 did that).
- Clustering closed bugs beyond using them as evidence for a family's recurrence.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The clustering is evidence-based
  Given the open backlog at the start of S23
  When the clustering report is delivered
  Then every cluster names its member issue keys and the shared root cause in one sentence
  And at least 70 percent of open defects are assigned to a cluster, with the remainder explicitly recorded as singletons

Scenario: A decision criterion is applied, not a preference
  Given a cluster with five members
  When the root-fix recommendation is made
  Then it states the estimated root-fix size, the estimated sum of local fixes, the blast radius of the root fix, and which is recommended and why
  And a root fix whose blast radius touches a trading-safety invariant is recommended only with a named guard test

Scenario: Test gaps are identified by layer
  Given a cluster classified as a test-gap family
  When the report describes it
  Then it names the specific pyramid layer that should have caught the family per docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md
  And it proposes one guard test at that layer covering the family

Scenario: The timebox is honoured
  Given the four-day timebox expires with two families unresolved
  Then the report records them as unresolved with what is known and what is missing
  And the ADR records a "defer, need more data" decision for those families with a follow-up ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Method: export the open backlog via the Projects v2 API into a dataframe (title, body, component, severity, originating epic, stack/area touched, linked PR files where a fix was attempted). Cluster manually with tooling assistance — affinity mapping by the QA lead plus one engineer per area — rather than by unsupervised text clustering alone, which reliably groups by vocabulary instead of by cause. Automated keyword grouping is used only to *propose* candidate groups for human confirmation.
- Evidence per cluster: at least two members reproduced and traced to the same code path, or an explicit note that the shared cause is hypothesised from symptoms.
- Blast-radius assessment uses the white-box checklist in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4 — particularly the OMS native-SL invariant clause — to flag clusters whose root fix touches safety-critical paths; those get stricter review and a named guard test.

title: Build the GA defect triage queue with enforced fields and SLA automation
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 defines a bug taxonomy with triage SLAs (P0 within 2 h, P1 within 1 business day, P2 within 3 business days, P3 within 1 sprint) and a rule that no bug closes "fixed" without a regression test guarding it. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.1 defines the Bug DoR — repro steps, expected vs actual, severity, root-cause hypothesis, the identified regression-test gap, and a link to the originating Story/Epic. Neither is machine-enforced today, so by R5 the backlog contains bugs that cannot be worked without going back to their reporter.

R5 exit criterion 3 is a numeric bar ("zero open P0/P1; open P2 ≤10 with owners and target sprints; open P3 triaged"). You cannot hit a numeric bar on a queue you cannot measure or trust. This ticket makes the queue trustworthy: one canonical view, enforced fields, automated SLA tracking, and a weekly triage ritual.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Canonical queue definition**: saved project views on the existing GitHub Project (schema per `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`) — "GA burn-down" (Kind=Bug, Status≠Done), "Untriaged", "SLA at risk", "Missing DoR", "By component", "By root-cause cluster". No new tracker, no new fields beyond the existing `Kind/Phase/Sprint/Component/Priority/Perspective/Risk/Estimate`.
- **Bug issue template refresh** enforcing the §6.1 DoR fields: exact repro steps, environment (dev/staging/prod, Demo/Live), symbol and account context, expected vs actual, severity with the §11.3 definition inline, root-cause hypothesis or needs-investigation flag, the test layer that should have caught it, and the originating Story/Epic key.
- **DoR validation bot**: a GitHub Action on issue open/edit that labels `needs-dor` and comments the specific missing fields when the template is incomplete; removes the label when satisfied. It never auto-closes.
- **SLA automation**: an Action that computes time-since-open for untriaged bugs and applies `sla-at-risk` at 75% of the severity's triage window and `sla-breached` past it, posting a daily digest to the team channel.
- **Regression-guard gate**: a check that blocks closing a Bug issue as completed unless the closing PR references a test file change, or the issue carries the explicit `p3-cosmetic-exempt` label with a stated reason (the §11.3 exemption).
- **Root-cause cluster field**: a label namespace `cluster/<name>` populated by E49-K01, so the waves can be planned by theme.
- **Weekly triage ritual**: a documented 45-minute ritual (attendees: QA lead, Architect, one engineer per area, designer for `design-qa` findings) with an agenda, a decision taxonomy (fix now / fix this wave / accept with owner+expiry / close as works-as-designed / re-file as post-GA Story) and a written record.
- **Import of existing debt**: a one-time sweep re-grading every open bug against §11.3 and tagging those that fail DoR.

## Out of scope
- Fixing any bug (the S-tickets).
- Replacing GitHub Issues/Projects with another tool.
- Changing the severity taxonomy itself — §11.3 is authoritative and unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An incomplete bug report is flagged immediately
  Given a new issue of Kind Bug is opened without repro steps
  When the DoR validation Action runs
  Then the issue is labelled needs-dor within two minutes
  And a comment names exactly which required fields are missing
  And the issue is not auto-closed

Scenario: An SLA breach is visible before it happens
  Given a P1 bug opened at 09:00 on a business day with a one-business-day triage window
  When 75 percent of the window has elapsed without a triage decision
  Then the issue is labelled sla-at-risk and appears in the daily digest
  And past the full window it is labelled sla-breached

Scenario: A bug cannot close without a guard
  Given a P2 bug whose closing PR changes only source files
  When the close is attempted
  Then the regression-guard check fails and names the requirement
  And the check passes once a test file change is included or the p3-cosmetic-exempt label with a reason is applied

Scenario: The existing debt is graded
  Given the open bug backlog at the start of S23
  When the one-time sweep completes
  Then every open bug carries a severity consistent with the §11.3 definitions
  And every bug failing the DoR carries needs-dor with a named owner to complete it

Scenario: Business hours are respected
  Given a P0 bug opened at 17:00 on a Friday with a two-hour business-hours triage window
  When the SLA clock is computed
  Then weekend hours are excluded and the deadline falls on the next business morning
```

## Technical notes / design
- Implementation: GitHub Actions in `.github/workflows/defect-triage.yml` plus a small Python helper in `tools/triage/` reusing the repo's existing Python 3.12 toolchain; GraphQL against the Projects v2 API for field reads/writes.
- Business-hours SLA arithmetic uses a configurable working calendar (`tools/triage/calendar.yml`: timezone, working days, working hours, holidays) — hard-coding a 24/7 clock would produce false breaches and train the team to ignore the labels.
- The regression-guard check is a required status check on the PR, not a bot comment, so it actually blocks.
- All automation is idempotent and rate-limit aware (Projects v2 API); failures are logged and retried with backoff, never silently swallowed.
- Config keys: `TRIAGE_PROJECT_ID`, `TRIAGE_DIGEST_WEBHOOK`, `TRIAGE_CALENDAR_PATH`. Error codes surfaced in the digest: `E_TRIAGE_API`, `E_TRIAGE_FIELD_MISSING`, `E_TRIAGE_RATE_LIMITED`.

## Test plan
- Unit: SLA clock arithmetic (business hours, weekend spillover, holiday, DST boundary, opened-outside-working-hours); DoR parser against fixture issue bodies (complete, each field missing individually, extra sections, non-template body); regression-guard PR-diff classifier (test file changed / only source changed / only docs changed / exempt label present).
- Integration: run the workflows against a scratch project board with seeded issues; assert labels applied and digest payload shape.
- Contract: Projects v2 GraphQL queries validated against the schema in CI so an API change fails loudly.
- E2E/perf/chaos: N/A, except an API-unavailable path test asserting retry-then-alert rather than silent failure.
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/triage/issues/*.md`, `tests/fixtures/triage/calendar.yml`.
- Coverage target: ≥85% (backend/tooling package gate).

## Security notes
The automation holds a token with project and issue write scope — a tampering and elevation-of-privilege surface per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Controls: a fine-grained token limited to this repository and the project, stored as a repository secret, never echoed in logs; workflows use `pull_request_target` only where unavoidable and never check out untrusted PR code with the token in scope; the digest webhook URL is a secret. Bug bodies may contain repro data — the template states that no API keys, session tokens or live account identifiers may be pasted, and the DoR bot runs a secret-pattern scan on the body and redacts-and-warns on a hit. Data classification: internal; potential incidental secrets, hence the scan.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no application UI. The digest message is plain text with no colour-only meaning so it remains readable in any client.

## Performance notes
Workflows must complete within 2 minutes per event and the daily digest within 5 minutes for a backlog of up to 2,000 issues; API calls are batched and paginated. No impact on the application's runtime budgets.

## Observability
- Metrics exported to the existing Prometheus stack via a pushgateway job: `defects_open{severity,component}`, `defects_untriaged{severity}`, `sla_breach_total{severity}`, `defect_age_days` histogram, `bugs_closed_without_guard_total` (should be zero).
- Structured logs from the helper with a correlation id per workflow run.
- The weekly triage record is committed to `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-triage-log.md` so decisions are auditable.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Views, template, bots and required check live and exercised on real issues.
- [ ] One-time re-grading sweep complete; counts published.
- [ ] Weekly ritual documented and run at least twice before S24 ends.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests green; coverage ≥85%.
- [ ] Security: token scope reviewed by the Security engineer; secret-scan path tested.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 cross-links the automation; triage ritual documented.
- [ ] Demo: the queue and digest shown at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
None inside this epic; it is the first ticket and everything else consumes its queue.

title: Publish the defect burn-down and ageing dashboard against the GA target line
body:
## Context
The R5 exit criteria in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 are numeric, and the train is four sprints long. Without a visible burn-down curve the team discovers in S26 that the S24 rate was insufficient. This ticket turns E49-T01's metrics into a Grafana view with a target line, so the Owner and the leads can see at any point whether GA is reachable and can re-plan a wave while re-planning is still cheap.

`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and the observability stories (US-OBS-001 metrics pipeline) already establish Prometheus + Grafana as the stack; this dashboard lives there rather than in a spreadsheet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Grafana dashboard "GA readiness — defects"** provisioned as code under `ops/grafana/dashboards/ga-defects.json`, panels:
  1. Open defects by severity over time, stacked, with a target line reaching zero P0/P1 and ≤10 P2 at the S26 boundary.
  2. Arrival vs closure rate per week (if arrivals exceed closures the curve cannot converge — this is the leading indicator).
  3. Ageing histogram by severity with the §11.3 SLA windows marked.
  4. Untriaged count and SLA-at-risk/breached counts.
  5. Defects by component, to reveal where the debt actually sits.
  6. `design_qa_findings_open{severity}` from the E49-D01 ledger, so design debt is visible next to functional debt.
  7. Forecast panel: linear and 3-week-trailing projections of the zero-crossing date against 2027-03-25.
- **Ledger exporter**: a small job that parses `e49-design-qa-ledger.csv` on each commit and pushes counts to the pushgateway.
- **Alert rules**: `GADefectForecastSlipping` (projected zero-crossing later than the S26 boundary for 3 consecutive days), `GADefectArrivalExceedsClosure` (7-day arrival rate > closure rate), `GADefectSLABreached` (any P0/P1 breach). Routed to the existing alerting path with runbook links.
- **Weekly snapshot** appended to `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-triage-log.md` so the history survives independently of Grafana retention.

## Out of scope
- Building the metric collection itself (E49-T01).
- Any new metrics backend or hosted service.
- Perf dashboards — **E46** owns those.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The curve and its target are both visible
  Given the dashboard is open at any point in S23 to S26
  When the burn-down panel renders
  Then the current open counts by severity and the target line to the S26 boundary are both shown
  And the projected zero-crossing date is stated numerically, not only as a line

Scenario: Divergence alerts before it is too late
  Given the 7-day arrival rate exceeds the 7-day closure rate
  When the alert rules evaluate
  Then GADefectArrivalExceedsClosure fires with the component breakdown in its annotation
  And the alert links to the triage ritual runbook

Scenario: Design debt is not hidden
  Given the design-QA ledger records 40 open findings
  When the ledger exporter runs on the ledger commit
  Then the dashboard shows design_qa_findings_open by severity within one scrape interval

Scenario: Missing data is visible as missing
  Given the pushgateway has received no update for over 2 hours
  When the dashboard renders
  Then panels show a stale-data indication rather than silently drawing the last value as current
```

## Technical notes / design
- Dashboards are provisioned as JSON in the repo and loaded by the existing Grafana provisioning config — no click-ops, so the dashboard is reviewable and restorable.
- Forecast: linear regression over the trailing 3 weeks of net open count, plus a naive last-week-rate projection; both shown, because a single projection invites false confidence. Neither is presented as a commitment.
- Stale-data handling uses the pushgateway's `push_time_seconds` compared against now, surfaced as an explicit panel state.
- Target line is a static series derived from the S26 boundary date and the exit-criteria numbers, defined in the dashboard JSON so it cannot drift from the roadmap silently.

## Test plan
- Unit: forecast functions tested against synthetic series (converging, flat, diverging, sparse, single-point) asserting sensible or explicitly-undefined output rather than a misleading extrapolation.
- Unit: ledger exporter parsing against the fixture ledgers from E49-D01, including malformed rows.
- Integration: provision the dashboard into a throwaway Grafana, push seeded metrics, assert panels resolve and alert rules evaluate as expected via the Grafana API.
- Chaos: pushgateway unavailable — exporter retries and the dashboard shows stale rather than stale-as-fresh.
- Coverage target: ≥85% on the exporter and forecast code.

The dashboard exposes no customer or trading data — only defect counts — so its classification is internal. The exporter reads a repository file and writes to the pushgateway; it holds no credentials beyond the pushgateway endpoint. The Grafana instance remains reachable only over Tailscale per the locked remote-access decision in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`; this ticket must not introduce any publicly reachable endpoint. The dashboard is an internal Grafana view but is still used by humans: panels must not encode severity by colour alone — each series is labelled, and the severity ordering is stated in the legend text. Alert annotations are plain sentences naming the metric, the threshold and the action.

## Performance notes
Dashboard queries must render within 3 s over a 4-sprint range; the exporter runs at most once per commit and once hourly, negligible load. No effect on application budgets.

This ticket *is* observability; it additionally exports `ga_defect_forecast_days_to_zero` so the forecast itself is alertable and historisable.

title: Re-review every accepted risk and enforce expiry dates before GA
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 exit criterion 4 is explicit: "Every accepted risk in `32-risk-register.md` has a current owner, an expiry date, and a review record; expired acceptances are re-decided, not silently extended." `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` §1.3 already mandates the cadence — full walkthrough at every train boundary and PRR, with "expired risk acceptances are re-decided, not extended", and a quarterly re-review of accepted risks against their expiry dates. R5 is the last train, so this is the final enforcement point before GA.

Risk acceptance decays. A risk accepted in R1 on the basis of "only the owner uses the system, on a tailnet, in demo" is a different decision once multiple managers trade live money. This task re-decides each acceptance against the *current* system rather than the one that existed when the acceptance was made.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Inventory** every entry in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` with Status `Accepted`, plus every accepted-risk sign-off recorded on tickets across E01–E48 (security findings triaged as accepted-risk per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2, pen-test findings accepted in **E43**, a11y non-conformances accepted in **E47**, perf budgets accepted as soft in **E46**, and design-QA exceptions accepted in E49-D05). Ticket-level acceptances that never made it into the register are the most likely gap and are explicitly hunted.
- **Per-acceptance re-review** producing one of four outcomes, each recorded with a date and a named decider: re-accept with a new expiry and a stated re-review trigger; mitigate now (file the work); escalate to the Owner for a GA-blocking decision; or retire because the risk no longer applies.
- **Field completion**: every accepted risk ends with a current owner (a role per `docs/plan/33-raci.md`, not a committee), an expiry date, a dated review record, and a concrete trigger that would move it from watched to active.
- **Re-scoring** of L and I against the current system, since scores set pre-live are frequently wrong post-live; the heat map in §2 is regenerated.
- **Register hygiene**: statuses reconciled with reality (a risk marked Mitigating whose mitigation shipped becomes Retired with the evidence linked); the §10.0.1 never-issued/retired ID list updated if any ID is retired here.
- **Expiry enforcement mechanism**: a check that parses the register and fails CI (or raises a scheduled alert post-GA) when an accepted risk's expiry date has passed, so the discipline survives the epic rather than depending on someone remembering.
- **Summary for the PRR**: a one-page accepted-risk statement for the GA PRR pack consumed by **E48** and `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Out of scope
- Performing the mitigations themselves; this task decides and files, it does not fix.
- Re-running the pen-test (**E43**) or the a11y audit (**E47**).
- Inventing new risks, beyond recording any that the re-review surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No acceptance survives without a current decision
  Given the set of accepted risks at the start of Sprint 25
  When the re-review completes
  Then each has a dated review record in Sprint 25 or later, a named owner role and an expiry date
  And none carries an expiry date that has already passed

Scenario: An expired acceptance is re-decided, not extended
  Given an acceptance whose expiry passed during R4
  When it is re-reviewed
  Then the outcome is recorded as re-accept with a new expiry and trigger, mitigate, escalate or retire
  And a bare extension of the old date without a recorded rationale is rejected in review

Scenario: Ticket-level acceptances are pulled into the register
  Given a security finding accepted on an E43 ticket that never reached the register
  When the inventory sweep runs
  Then it appears in the register with owner, expiry, trigger and a link to its originating ticket

Scenario: The enforcement check actually blocks
  Given the register contains an accepted risk with an expiry date in the past
  When the expiry check runs in CI
  Then it fails naming the risk id, its owner and the elapsed days

Scenario: Re-scoring can raise a GA blocker
  Given a risk accepted at score 6 under demo-only conditions
  When it is re-scored against multi-manager live trading and reaches 15
  Then it is escalated to the Owner as a GA decision rather than silently re-accepted
```

## Technical notes / design
- The register is markdown with a stable table structure; the expiry check parses the risk entries by their `### RSK-nnn` headings and their field lines, failing loudly on an unparseable entry rather than skipping it (a skipped entry is exactly the one that would hide an expired acceptance).
- Post-GA the same check runs on a schedule and raises an alert through the existing alerting path, implementing §1.3's quarterly cadence mechanically.
- The re-review is run as two working sessions: one with the Security engineer and Architect for R4/R5/R6/R11/R15-class risks, one with the Owner and QA lead for the remainder, since the accept decision for money-and-safety risks belongs to different people than the accept decision for scope or operability risks.
- Each outcome writes into the register in the same PR as the decision, so the register is never a lagging record.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: the register parser against fixture registers (well-formed, missing expiry, missing owner, past expiry, unparseable entry, retired entry) asserting correct pass/fail and a clear message in each case.
- **Integration**: run the check against the real register in CI; assert a seeded past-expiry entry fails the build.
- **Process verification**: the completeness of the inventory is verified by sampling ten tickets across E01–E48 that recorded an accepted-risk sign-off and confirming each appears in the register.
- **Coverage**: ≥85% on the checking script.

## Security notes
This task is a compliance control for `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`'s accepted-risk process. Threats it addresses: repudiation (an acceptance with no named decider or date cannot be defended after an incident) and silent risk drift (an acceptance made under old assumptions carried into live multi-manager trading). The re-review must be conducted against the *current* threat model, including the changes introduced by **E44** live enablement and **E43** hardening. Security-sensitive acceptances require the Security engineer's signature, not merely their presence in the session. The register itself is internal and contains no secrets, but it does describe weaknesses — it stays in the private repository and is not published in any GA artefact that leaves the tailnet.

The one-page PRR statement lists them explicitly so the accessibility position is stated, not buried.

## Performance notes
Soft performance budgets accepted rather than met in **E46** are in scope: each is recorded as an accepted risk with its measured value, its budget, an owner and an expiry, so "we accepted this" is traceable rather than folkloric.

## Observability
