title: Add a CI lint that proves the keymap is conflict-free in every context
body:
## Context
US-SET-002 (Must) requires "one remappable hotkey scheme across every view, so that muscle memory always works", with three scenarios: a remapped binding works in every view where the action is valid and is inert elsewhere *with an explanation on press*; a colliding binding is shown with both actions and must be resolved before saving; and a key reserved by the OS or browser is refused with the reason. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-113 (hotkey editor) specifies per-context conflict detection with the conflicting command named, and a safety group where destructive commands (flatten, cancel-all, freeze) can be required to use a modifier or be unbound. SCR-013 is the cheatsheet that renders the user's current bindings grouped by context (Global, Chart, DOM, Ticket, Replay, Rules).

The *default* keymap is the part nobody re-checks. Fifteen epics added bindings independently — SCR-030 chart (`F`, `Alt+F`, `1..9`, `Ctrl+drag`, `Alt+click`, `Esc`, `Del`, `Ctrl+Z/Y`), SCR-050/051 DOM (`Ctrl+click`, `Shift+click`, `Esc`, `+/-`, `C`, `Space`, `Ctrl+Shift+T`), SCR-060 ticket (`B`/`S`, `1..4`, `Ctrl+Enter`, `Esc`, `Alt+B`/`Alt+A`, `Alt+M`, `R`, `Ctrl+Shift+T`), SCR-070 positions (`Enter`, `Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+Shift+W`), replay (`Space`, `←/→`, `Shift+←/→`, `Ctrl+←/→`, `R`, `B`, `[`/`]`), rule editors (`Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+Enter`, `Alt+G`, `Alt+↑/↓`, `Ctrl+D`, `Del`, `Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+G`, `Ctrl+L`, `Tab`, `Enter`, `F2`), plus global (`Ctrl+K`, `Ctrl+Shift+A`, `Ctrl+/`, `F11`, `Alt+1..9`). Some of those collide by design across contexts and some collide by accident.

This task builds the machine check so the audit in E49-S07 has an oracle and so conflicts cannot silently return.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Single keymap source of truth**: a declarative keymap file (`packages/web/src/keymap/keymap.ts` or equivalent) enumerating every command with its id, human label, context (Global, Chart, DOM, Ticket, Positions, Replay, Rules, Admin, Settings), default binding, destructive flag and validity predicate. Bindings scattered in component code are migrated into it; the components read from it.
- **Conflict lint** (`scripts/keymap_lint`): fails CI when two commands share a binding within the same context, or when a context-scoped binding shadows a Global binding without an explicit `shadows:` declaration justifying it, or when a destructive command has a single-letter binding while the safety option is on by default.
- **Reserved-key list**: bindings reserved by the OS, the browser and the Electron shell (`Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+T`, `Ctrl+Shift+I`, `F5`, `Alt+F4`, platform equivalents), with the lint failing on any default binding that collides — except where the app deliberately overrides it and records the override and its rationale (`Ctrl+W` for close-position on SCR-070 is exactly such a case and must be an explicit, reviewed decision, not an accident).
- **Coverage check**: every command in the keymap appears in the SCR-013 cheatsheet data and is editable in SCR-113; every binding referenced in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`'s Interactions/hotkeys lines exists in the keymap. Drift in either direction fails.
- **Docs generator**: emits a markdown table of the default keymap for **E48**'s user guide, so the documented keymap cannot diverge from the shipped one.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the conflicts found — E49-S07.
- Changing the runtime conflict-detection UI in SCR-113, which already exists per US-SET-002; this task validates *defaults* at build time.
- Adding new commands or new hotkeys.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A same-context collision fails the build
  Given two commands in the Chart context both bound to the letter F
  When the keymap lint runs
  Then CI fails naming both command ids, the context and the binding

Scenario: Deliberate cross-context reuse is allowed but declared
  Given Escape cancels an in-progress drawing in Chart and cancels working orders in DOM
  When the lint runs
  Then it passes because each declares the other in its shadows list with a rationale
  And an undeclared cross-context shadow of a Global binding fails

Scenario: A reserved key is caught
  Given a default binding uses Ctrl+Shift+I
  When the lint runs
  Then CI fails naming the reserving platform
  And an intentional override passes only when it carries a written rationale in the keymap entry

Scenario: The catalogue and the keymap cannot drift
  Given docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md documents a hotkey that no keymap entry defines
  When the coverage check runs
  Then CI fails naming the screen and the undocumented or undefined binding

Scenario: Destructive commands are protected by default
  Given the safety option defaults to requiring a modifier for destructive commands
  When a destructive command's default binding is a bare single letter
  Then the lint fails naming the command
```

## Technical notes / design
- The keymap is data, not code paths: a command declares `{id, label, context, defaultBinding, destructive, shadows?, reservedOverride?, validWhen}`. Components resolve behaviour through a dispatcher keyed by command id, which also makes US-SET-002's "inert elsewhere with an explanation on press" implementable in one place rather than per view.
- Binding normalisation handles modifier order, platform differences (`Ctrl` vs `Cmd`), and key-vs-code distinctions so that `Ctrl+Shift+F` and `Shift+Ctrl+F` compare equal and layout-dependent keys are compared by physical code where appropriate.
- The lint is a plain script run in the `contracts`-style CI job so its failures are blocking and readable.
- The catalogue cross-check parses the `**Interactions/hotkeys:**` lines from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`; parsing is deliberately strict and any unparseable line is reported rather than skipped, so the check cannot pass by failing to see things.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: normalisation (modifier order, platform mapping, key vs code); collision detection (same context, cross-context declared and undeclared, global shadowing); reserved-key detection with and without a rationale; destructive-binding rule; catalogue parser against fixture lines including malformed ones.
- **Integration**: run the lint against the real keymap in CI; run the docs generator and assert the output is stable and deterministic.
- **Contract**: the coverage check *is* a contract test between the keymap, SCR-013's data source and the screens catalogue.
- **Coverage**: ≥80% frontend package gate.

## Security notes
Hotkeys are a safety surface: rebinding a trading action changes the risk profile of muscle memory, which is why `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-113 audits `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`. This task must not weaken that — the destructive-command safety default stays on, and the lint enforces it. A binding that could fire a destructive trading action with a single unmodified key is treated as a safety defect, not a usability preference. No new attack surface; no secrets touched.

## Accessibility notes
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires every screen to be fully operable keyboard-only, and SCR-113 requires a keyboard-only alternative to key capture (choosing modifiers plus key from selects). The lint additionally flags any command whose only invocation path is a hotkey with no equivalent visible control, because that would make the action unreachable for users who cannot use that key combination — such commands must either gain a control or declare an exception with rationale.

## Performance notes
Conflict detection at runtime is an O(1) lookup against the binding map per SCR-113's performance note; moving bindings into one map preserves that. The lint is build-time only and adds under 5 s to CI.

## Observability
The docs generator's output is committed, so a keymap change shows up as a reviewable diff. Runtime analytics (`hotkey.changed`, `hotkey.reset`, `hotkey.profile_imported`, and the audited `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`) are unchanged by this task.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Keymap source of truth landed; component-local bindings migrated.
- [ ] Conflict, reserved-key, destructive-safety and coverage checks live and CI-blocking.
- [ ] Docs generator emits the default-keymap table for E48.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests green; coverage ≥80%.
- [ ] security: destructive-binding default reviewed and preserved.
- [ ] a11y: hotkey-only commands identified and either given a control or declared with rationale.
- [ ] Docs: keymap file documented; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` cross-checked.
- [ ] Demo: lint failing on a seeded conflict shown at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
None blocking; it is a prerequisite for E49-S07.

## Branch
`chore/e49-keymap-lint` · PR size: one PR to introduce the keymap and migrate bindings, one for the lint and generator.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-002 (global hotkey layer), US-ORD-006.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010, SCR-012, SCR-013, SCR-113, and the Interactions/hotkeys lines of SCR-030, SCR-050, SCR-051, SCR-060, SCR-070, SCR-100 band and the rule editors.

title: Reconcile plan docs with shipped behaviour and write the defect-disposition ADR
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires that an epic's docs "reflect final shipped behavior (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation", and §6.2 requires docs updates where a bug revealed a spec inaccuracy. A burn-down epic generates exactly that kind of divergence in bulk: every root-cause fix that changed behaviour, every state-pattern conformance fix, every copy change, and every hotkey rebind makes some sentence in the plan docs untrue.

Separately, the epic's central judgement — what "a defensible defect level" means and how the surviving exceptions were decided — needs to be recorded as an ADR rather than living in a sprint report, because it is the policy that a future maintainer will be measured against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` — *GA defect disposition policy*: the numeric bar (zero P0/P1; ≤10 P2 each with owner, impact statement and target sprint; all P3 triaged), the regression-guard requirement and its narrow cosmetic exemption, the rule that the bar may not be met by re-grading (with the downgrade count published), the themes-over-symptoms clustering rule, the change-freeze policy from S26 week 2, and the post-GA triage cadence that inherits from this epic. Consequences and rejected alternatives stated honestly.
- **Doc reconciliation sweep** driven by the merged fix list:
  - `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — states, hotkeys, interactions and analytics lines corrected where remediation changed them.
  - `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — variant and state additions arising from E49-S04/S05; no new CMP ids.
  - `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` — acceptance criteria annotated where shipped behaviour legitimately differs, with the divergence and its rationale recorded rather than the story silently rewritten.
  - `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` — error-registry message and shape changes from E49-S06; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` where a root fix changed a domain event or state machine.
  - `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` where a fix required a migration.
  - `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` where a root fix moved a responsibility between modules.
  - `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 cross-linking the triage automation from E49-T01.
  - `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` already updated by E49-T03; this sweep only verifies consistency.
- **Divergence log** `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-doc-divergences.md`: every doc change with the fix that caused it, so the reconciliation is auditable and **E48** can cite it.
- **Consistency check** extending the existing `docs` CI job: no dangling `SCR-`, `CMP-`, `US-` or `RSK-` reference; every referenced API path and WS topic exists in the contract; every ADR referenced by a doc exists in the index.

## Out of scope
- Authoring the user guide, runbooks, API reference publication or the onboarding guide — all **E48**.
- Rewriting historical sprint reports.
- Changing product decisions; this records what shipped, it does not re-litigate it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every behavioural fix is reflected or explicitly deemed immaterial
  Given the list of fixes merged in this epic that changed user-visible behaviour
  When the reconciliation sweep completes
  Then each has either a corresponding doc change or an entry in the divergence log stating why no doc change was needed

Scenario: The ADR states a policy, not a narrative
  Given the GA defect-disposition ADR
  When it is reviewed by the Architect and the QA lead
  Then it states the numeric bar, the guard requirement, the exemption, the anti-regrading rule, the freeze policy and the post-GA cadence
  And it records the alternatives considered and why they were rejected

Scenario: Dangling references fail the build
  Given a doc references SCR-999 which does not exist
  When the docs consistency check runs
  Then CI fails naming the file, the line and the missing id

Scenario: The contract and the docs agree
  Given a doc references an API path or WS topic
  When the check runs
  Then the path exists in docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml or the topic exists in docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md
  And a reference to a removed endpoint fails the build

Scenario: A story's shipped behaviour differs legitimately
  Given US-SET-002's inert-hotkey behaviour was refined during E49-S07
  When the story is reconciled
  Then the divergence and its rationale are recorded alongside the original acceptance criteria
  And the original criteria are not deleted, so the history of the decision survives
```

## Technical notes / design
- The fix list is generated from the epic's closed tickets and their merged PRs (title, touched paths, user-visible flag set during triage), so the sweep has a definite input rather than relying on recollection.
- The consistency check is a Python script in the existing `docs` CI job: it extracts `SCR-\d+`, `CMP-\d+`, `US-[A-Z]+-\d+`, `RSK-\d+`, `ADR-\d+` references and resolves them against their catalogues, and resolves API paths and WS topic names against the contract files. Unresolvable-by-design references (illustrative examples) must be marked with an inline annotation, not silently tolerated.
- Story reconciliation is additive: divergences are appended to the story with a dated note, because deleting the original criteria destroys the record of what was agreed and why it changed.
- The ADR follows the existing `docs/plan/27-adrs/` format and is added to the ADR index.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: the reference extractor and resolver against fixture docs (valid reference, dangling reference, annotated illustrative reference, malformed id, reference inside a code block that should be ignored or not per the rule).
- **Integration**: run the check against the real docs tree in CI; assert a seeded dangling reference fails.
- **Review**: the divergence log is reviewed by someone who did not write the fixes, per R5's docs quality gate ("docs reviewed by someone who did not write them", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4).
- **Coverage**: ≥85% on the check script.

## Security notes
Documentation can leak. The sweep must not introduce internal hostnames, tailnet addresses, real account identifiers, key material or specific unmitigated-weakness detail into documents that will be handed to a future engineer as part of **E48**'s onboarding guide. The risk register's weakness descriptions stay in the private repository. The divergence log references ticket keys rather than pasting bug bodies, which may contain repro data. Reviewed as part of the E49-X02 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
Doc changes describing accessibility behaviour must match what shipped — an aspirational a11y sentence in the screens catalogue that no longer reflects the built behaviour is a conformance-evidence defect, not a typo, since **E47**'s conformance report cites these documents. Any such mismatch found is corrected here and flagged to E47.

## Performance notes
Performance numbers quoted in the screens catalogue (for example SCR-150's ≤2.5 s cold start, SCR-154's ≤200 ms render, SCR-152's ≤5 s time-to-usable) are reconciled against the measurements **E46** recorded, so documented budgets and enforced budgets agree. Where they differ, the enforced value wins and the doc is corrected.

## Observability
No runtime telemetry. The docs consistency check's failures are CI-visible, and the divergence log is the audit trail for the reconciliation.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` and added to the index.
- [ ] Every affected plan doc reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Divergence log complete and reviewed by someone who did not write the fixes.
- [ ] Docs consistency check live and CI-blocking; zero dangling references.
- [ ] Documented performance numbers reconciled with E46's enforced budgets.
- [ ] Documented a11y behaviour reconciled with E47's conformance report.
- [ ] Tests green; coverage ≥85%.
- [ ] Demo: not required (documentation task) — before/after diff summary attached instead.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E49-S03**, **E49-S05**, **E49-S06** — the fixes must be merged before their documentation effects can be reconciled.
- **E46** and **E47** publish the measured budgets and conformance verdicts this sweep reconciles against.
- **E48** consumes the reconciled docs and the ADR for the GA readiness pack.

## Branch
`docs/e49-reconciliation` · PR size: one PR for the ADR, one for the consistency check, one or two for the doc sweep grouped by document family.

## References
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2, §4.2, §6.2 (docs clauses).
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3, §9.4 (docs gate).
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR format and index).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `11-user-stories.md`, `20-architecture.md`, `21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `32-risk-register.md`.

title: Burn down wave 1: close every open P0 and the highest-impact P1 clusters
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 defines P0 as data loss, incorrect order execution or sizing, a missing native stop-loss, a security breach, or a crash blocking a core trading flow — and states P0s "must fix before any further merge to the affected area; blocks release". P1 is a major feature broken with a workaround, or a chaos scenario handled incorrectly, and "must fix before the current release gate". R5 exit criterion 3 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3) is zero open P0 and P1 at GA.

Wave 1 is the first of three burn-down waves and takes the most dangerous work first, while there are still three sprints of runway for the regressions a risky fix might cause. Its content is ordered by the cluster report from E49-K01: P0s individually, then the P1 clusters with the largest member counts and the clearest shared root causes.

As the owner of this epic's most safety-critical fixes, this story is where the trading-safety invariants get re-proven: the native-SL invariant, order sizing correctness, RBAC enforcement and book integrity.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Every open P0** at the start of S23, closed with a root-cause fix and a regression guard. Expected families, based on the §11.3 examples and the risk register's high-score entries: fan-out order missing a native SL (RSK-016), wrong position size submitted, auth or RBAC bypass (RSK-020, RSK-021), book corruption reaching the rule engine (RSK-010), orphaned or duplicated orders after a crash (RSK-017).
- **The top P1 clusters** identified by E49-K01, targeted at root cause with one guard test per family. Expected candidates: WS reconnect failing to reconcile fully (RSK-010, and the sequence in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §9.1), rule-editor round-trip losing a field, chart-engine panes rendering incorrect non-trading data, emulated-algo orphan cleanup after restart.
- **Guard tests** at the layer named in each bug's test-gap field: property-based tests for book/bar/footprint/CVD math and rule IR per §11.4; contract tests for any endpoint or WS topic implicated; integration tests against recorded Bybit fixtures; chaos scenarios re-run for reconnect families.
- **Incident notes** for every P0/P1 closed, feeding `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` per its §1.3 cadence.
- **Wave report** appended to `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-triage-log.md`: what was closed, what was deferred to wave 2 and why.

## Out of scope
- P2 and P3 defects — waves 2 and 3 (E49-S02, E49-S03).
- Design-QA, state-pattern, copy and hotkey findings — E49-S04…S07, even where they are technically P1, because they are a different skill mix and are tracked separately.
- Performance defects (routed to **E46**) and accessibility defects (routed to **E47**) per E49-K01's routing decisions.
- Any fix requiring new product capability — re-filed as a post-GA Story.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No P0 survives the wave
  Given the set of open P0 bugs at the start of Sprint 23
  When wave 1 closes at the end of Sprint 23
  Then every one of them is Done with a merged root-cause fix
  Or is explicitly re-classified with the reasoning recorded and the Owner's agreement

Scenario: Every closed bug is guarded
  Given a P0 or P1 closed in this wave
  When its regression test is run against the commit immediately preceding the fix
  Then the test fails
  And against the fix commit it passes

Scenario: The native stop-loss invariant is re-proven
  Given any fix in this wave touching the order-submission or fan-out path
  When the test suite runs
  Then a test asserts that every fanned-out order carries a native exchange-side stop-loss
  And the fix cannot merge without that assertion present

Scenario: A fix causes a regression elsewhere
  Given a wave 1 fix merges and the nightly GA regression pack subsequently fails in an unrelated area
  When the failure is triaged
  Then the regression is filed at the severity of the broken area and linked to the causing fix
  And the wave is not reported as closed until that regression is resolved or explicitly accepted by the Owner

Scenario: A root fix is too risky to land in one PR
  Given a cluster whose root fix would exceed 400 LOC or touch a trading-safety invariant broadly
  When the fix is planned
  Then it is split into reviewable increments, each independently revertible and independently tested
  And the increments land behind a feature flag whose default state is recorded on the ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Each fix follows `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2: root cause fixed, or a deliberate symptom patch with a follow-up Task filed; a regression test added at the layer identified in the bug's DoR test-gap field, proven to fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.
- PRs stay ≤400 LOC per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; one cluster or one bug per PR; never batch unrelated fixes, because a mixed PR cannot be reverted cleanly during a GA train.
- Cluster fixes touching the OMS order-submission path must preserve the native-SL-on-every-fanned-out-order invariant with an explicit asserting test (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4).
- Every merged fix runs the full required-check set including E46's CI-enforced performance budgets; a >5% regression on any hard budget fails the build (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4).
- Incident notes are written for every P0 and P1 per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2, capturing detection-to-fix timeline, and feed `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: one regression test per closed bug at the identified layer; property-based tests extended for any math or IR family per §11.4.
- **Contract**: schemathesis operations re-run for any REST endpoint touched; WS JSON-Schema cases for any topic touched (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`).
- **Integration**: recorded Bybit fixtures replayed for ingestion, book and OMS families; the §9.1 WS reconnect/reconciliation sequence re-executed for any reconnect fix.
- **E2E**: Playwright web + Electron scenarios added for any user-visible P0/P1; these become part of the GA regression pack (E49-Q01).
- **Chaos**: for reconnect, 5xx, rate-limit `10018` and crash-recovery families, the corresponding scenario from `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §9 is re-run green.
- **Perf**: E46's budget checks are required; hot-path fixes record before/after numbers on the ticket.
- **Fixtures**: existing `packages/fixtures` recorded sessions; new fixtures only where an existing one cannot reproduce, and then committed with provenance.
- **Coverage**: ≥85% backend/engine, ≥80% frontend, no package baseline regression.

## Security notes
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, any fix touching auth/RBAC, API-key storage, order-placement paths, withdrawal settings or the fan-out SL invariant is treated as `security`-labelled whether or not the label was applied, and cannot reach Done without a Security-engineer review comment. For this wave specifically: a fix for an auth or RBAC bypass requires a negative-authorization test (the disallowed action is actually rejected, not merely that the allowed one succeeds); a fix touching `api_keys` must preserve envelope encryption and must not add plaintext to logs, UI or error messages; the Security engineer additionally reviews each such fix for *related exposure elsewhere* per §6.2, since a bypass rarely has exactly one instance. Threats: tampering (a rushed fix bypassing review), elevation of privilege (an incomplete RBAC fix), information disclosure (key material in a new error path). Data classification: secrets, financial state, PII.

## Accessibility notes
Any P0/P1 with a UI surface re-enters the a11y gate on its touched screens: axe-core CI green, keyboard-only path verified, focus order and visible focus checked against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. A crash-boundary fix must preserve SCR-156's `role="alert"` region and the technical-detail disclosure pattern. A fix that changes an error string must preserve or improve the accessible name.

## Performance notes
E46's CI-enforced budgets are required checks on every PR in this wave. Fixes in the chart engine, book application, bar building or fan-out serialisation record a before/after benchmark on the ticket. A fix that trades correctness for a budget breach is not acceptable: if a correct fix breaches a budget, that is escalated to E46 as a joint item rather than silently shipped or silently reverted.

## Observability
- Wave progress is read from E49-T02's dashboard, filtered by `cluster/*`.
- Fixes that close a detection gap add the missing signal: a metric or structured log that would have surfaced the defect earlier (for example a counter for orders submitted without a native SL, which must be zero, alerted at >0).
- Incident notes are linked from the risk register entries they inform.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every open P0 closed or Owner-agreed re-classified; wave report published.
- [ ] Top P1 clusters closed at root cause with one guard test per family.
- [ ] Each closed bug has a regression test proven to fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.
- [ ] Native-SL invariant test present on every order-path fix.
- [ ] Coverage gates green; no package baseline regression.
- [ ] a11y gate green on every touched screen.
- [ ] perf: no E46 budget regression; before/after recorded for hot-path fixes.
- [ ] security: Security-engineer review on every security-touching fix, incl. related-exposure check.
- [ ] QA sign-off: repro steps re-verified as non-reproducing plus an adjacent-area regression sweep per §6.2.
- [ ] Incident notes written for every P0/P1; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated.
- [ ] Docs updated where a bug revealed a spec inaccuracy.
- [ ] All PRs merged via merge queue with required approvals.

## Dependencies
- **E49-K01** supplies the cluster ordering and root-fix recommendations; working wave 1 without it means fixing symptoms in an arbitrary order.
- **E49-T01** supplies the DoR-complete queue.
- **E43** — residual pen-test findings entering the queue are triaged into this wave if they are P0/P1.

## Branch
`fix/<area>-<short>` per bug or per cluster · PR size ≤400 LOC; risky root fixes split into independently revertible increments behind a recorded feature flag.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **All remaining open P1s** at the start of S24, closed at root cause per the E49-K01 cluster plan, each with a regression guard.
- **P1s arising from E49-Q02** exploratory charters (OMS/order path, rule-engine boundaries, fan-out edges, chart-engine visual correctness at extreme density, admin/RBAC probing) and the two bug bashes.

- **Regression closure**: any regression introduced by wave 1 is closed here, with an analysis note on why the wave-1 guard test did not cover it.

- **Wave report** appended to the triage log with closed/deferred counts and the updated forecast.

## Out of scope

```gherkin
  When it is closed in wave 2
  Then the ticket records why the wave 1 guard test did not detect it
  And the guard test is broadened, or a new test at a different layer is added

Scenario: Charter findings are not lost
  Given an exploratory charter debrief lists five candidate defects
  When triage runs

  And no candidate remains in the debrief note without a disposition

Scenario: A routed defect is rejected by the receiving epic
  Given a defect routed to E46 as a performance issue
  When E46 declines it as out of its scope
  Then it returns to this wave with its severity intact and is scheduled, not left in limbo
```

## Technical notes / design
- Each fix follows `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2: root cause fixed, or a deliberate symptom patch with a follow-up Task filed; a regression test added at the layer identified in the bug's DoR test-gap field, proven to fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.

- Incident notes are written for every P0 and P1 per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2, capturing detection-to-fix timeline, and feed `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: a regression test per closed bug at the identified layer; broadened guards for wave-1 escapes.
- **Contract**: re-run schemathesis and WS schema cases for any touched surface.
- **Integration**: recorded-fixture replays for ingestion/book/OMS/rule families.
- **E2E**: Playwright web + Electron additions for user-visible P1s, folded into E49-Q01's regression pack.
- **Chaos**: the full §9 catalogue re-run on the wave-2 build; every previously-amber scenario green and added to the nightly run.

title: Burn down wave 3: bring open P2s to the GA bar and triage every P3
body:
## Context
R5 exit criterion 3 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 is precise: "Zero open P0/P1 bugs; open P2 count ≤10 with owners and target sprints; open P3 triaged." Waves 1 and 2 handled P0/P1. Wave 3 is the P2 sweep plus the P3 triage discipline that makes "triaged" mean something.

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 defines P2 as a partially-broken feature, non-blocking, cosmetic-but-confusing, or an accessibility AA violation — "should fix before release; may be scheduled next sprint with owner sign-off". The GA bar accepts up to ten such items, but only with a named owner and a target sprint, which is what stops the category from becoming a landfill.

Wave 3 runs in S25, leaving S26 for verification, the GA regression pack and sign-offs rather than for fixing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **P2 sweep**: fix P2s in cluster order until the open count is ≤10, prioritising by (a) cluster size, (b) user-facing frequency evidenced by the analytics in E49-D02's event list (`empty_state_shown`, `error.403_shown`, `error.404_shown`, `app.error_boundary_triggered`, `degraded.entered`, `ratelimit.hit`), and (c) proximity to trading-critical surfaces.
- **The surviving ≤10 P2s**: each given a named owner, a written user-impact statement, a target post-GA sprint and an Owner sign-off, recorded on the ticket per §11.3's "may be scheduled next sprint with owner sign-off".
- **P3 triage pass**: every open P3 reviewed and given a disposition — fix now (cheap and adjacent to work already in flight), keep in backlog with a target, or close as won't-fix with a one-line reason. No P3 remains untouched.
- **Accessibility AA P2s**: verified as routed to and accepted by **E47**, or fixed here where E47 has closed and the finding is residual.
- **Batch fixes for trivial clusters**: P3 cosmetic items sharing a root (a spacing token, a truncation rule, a tooltip pattern) fixed together, using the `p3-cosmetic-exempt` regression-guard exemption only where a test genuinely adds no value, with the reason stated per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3.
- **Final forecast check** and wave report in the triage log.

## Out of scope
- P0/P1 work (waves 1 and 2) — any new P0/P1 raised during S25 is handled under the wave-1/2 rules and the freeze policy, not absorbed silently here.
- Design-QA, state, copy and hotkey remediation — E49-S04…S07, even though many are P2-severity, because they are tracked as their own ledgers.
- Any P2 whose fix requires new capability — re-filed as a post-GA Story.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The P2 bar is met with evidence
  Given the open P2 set at the end of Sprint 25
  When the count is reported on the burn-down dashboard
  Then at most 10 P2 bugs remain open
  And each has a named owner, a user-impact statement, a target post-GA sprint and a recorded Owner sign-off

Scenario: Every P3 has a disposition
  Given the open P3 backlog
  When the triage pass completes
  Then every P3 carries one of: scheduled with a target, kept with an explicit backlog disposition, or closed won't-fix with a reason
  And a query for untriaged P3s returns zero results

Scenario: Frequency evidence drives priority, not taste
  Given two P2 bugs of equal cluster size
  When they are prioritised
  Then the one whose surface shows the higher analytics occurrence rate is scheduled first
  And the ordering rationale is recorded so it can be challenged

Scenario: A cosmetic exemption is not a loophole
  Given a P3 closed using the p3-cosmetic-exempt label
  When the closure is reviewed
  Then the label carries a written reason explaining why a regression test adds no value
  And any exemption used on a non-cosmetic change is rejected in review

Scenario: The bar is reached by fixing, not by re-grading
  Given the P2 count is above 10 late in Sprint 25
  When a bug's severity is proposed for downgrade
  Then the downgrade requires the QA lead's agreement against the section 11.3 definition
  And downgrades are counted and reported in the wave report so the bar cannot be met by relabelling
```

## Technical notes / design
- Each fix follows `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2: root cause fixed, or a deliberate symptom patch with a follow-up Task filed; a regression test added at the layer identified in the bug's DoR test-gap field, proven to fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.
- PRs stay ≤400 LOC per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; one cluster or one bug per PR; never batch unrelated fixes, because a mixed PR cannot be reverted cleanly during a GA train.
- Cluster fixes touching the OMS order-submission path must preserve the native-SL-on-every-fanned-out-order invariant with an explicit asserting test (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4).
- Every merged fix runs the full required-check set including E46's CI-enforced performance budgets; a >5% regression on any hard budget fails the build (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4).
- Incident notes are written for every P0 and P1 per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2, capturing detection-to-fix timeline, and feed `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: a regression test per closed P2 at its identified layer; cosmetic P3 exemptions used only where justified.
- **Visual regression**: for token/spacing/truncation clusters, screenshot-comparison tests on the affected Storybook stories, so a cosmetic cluster gets one mechanical guard rather than none.
- **Contract/integration**: re-run for any touched surface.
- **E2E**: additions for user-visible P2s on trading-critical surfaces, folded into E49-Q01.
- **A11y**: axe-core and pa11y-ci on every touched screen; AA violations are P2 minimum per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12.
- **Perf**: E46 budget checks required.
- **Coverage**: ≥85% backend/engine, ≥80% frontend; no baseline regression.

## Security notes
P2s rarely look like security work, which is exactly the risk. Reviewers apply `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8: a "cosmetic" change to a 403 or 404 message, an error string, a tooltip on an admin surface, or a disabled-control reason can become an information-disclosure defect. Specific checks in this wave: 403/404 copy must not reveal whether an admin-only resource exists (SCR-154, SCR-155); error strings must not gain raw exception text or internal hostnames; a fix that makes a disabled control's reason more specific must not leak another user's or account's state. Any P2 touching auth, keys, OMS or RBAC gets the full security gate regardless of its cosmetic appearance.

## Accessibility notes
Accessibility AA violations are P2 by policy (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12), so this wave carries real a11y content. Every fix re-runs axe-core on its screen, verifies the keyboard-only path, checks focus order and visible focus per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, and preserves accessible names. Residual a11y items not fixed here must be accepted by **E47** with a written non-conformance entry in its conformance report, not left implicit.

## Performance notes
E46's budgets are required checks. Visual-regression tests must run on the reference configuration and not in a degraded rendering mode, or they produce false diffs. A cosmetic fix that adds a layout-thrashing style is a perf regression and is caught by the budget check, not waved through as "just CSS".

## Observability
- The dashboard's P2/P3 series is the acceptance instrument for this wave; the wave report cites the dashboard at the S25 boundary.
- Downgrade count is published explicitly, so the bar's integrity is auditable.
- Analytics occurrence rates used for prioritisation are recorded on the tickets, making the ordering reproducible.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Open P2 count ≤10, each with owner, impact statement, target sprint and Owner sign-off.
- [ ] Every P3 triaged with a recorded disposition; zero untriaged.
- [ ] Regression guard per closed bug, or a justified cosmetic exemption.
- [ ] Visual-regression guards added for cosmetic clusters.
- [ ] a11y gate green on touched screens; residual items accepted by E47 in writing.
- [ ] perf: no E46 budget regression.
- [ ] security: §8 gating applied; disclosure checks performed on copy and state changes.
- [ ] QA sign-off with repro re-verification and adjacent sweep.
- [ ] Wave report published including the downgrade count and the final forecast.
- [ ] All PRs merged via merge queue.

title: Remediate design-QA findings across the screens catalogue against the specs
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12 requires that every screen use only published Tier-2/Tier-3 tokens with zero hardcoded hex or px values, be verified in dark, light and high-contrast at compact and comfortable density, pass the contrast matrix, have a Figma variant and a Storybook story per documented state, use the disabled-with-reason pattern (CMP-079) for RBAC/env-gated controls, meet hit-target minimums, chip-tag every estimated value, and reuse an existing `CMP-*` rather than a near-duplicate. E49-D01 audited the catalogue against exactly that checklist and produced a per-screen findings ledger with severities.

This story executes the remediation. It is the engineering half of the design-QA sweep named in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 for E49, and it feeds E49-D05's final sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Token conformance**: replace hardcoded colour, spacing, radius, elevation, type and motion values with the published tokens from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §2; add an ESLint/stylelint rule banning raw hex and raw px in component styles so the class of defect cannot return.
- **Theme and density parity**: fix layout breakage found in high-contrast and in compact density; verify each remediated screen across all six theme × density combinations.
- **Contrast fixes**: resolve every contrast-matrix failure recorded in the ledger, including order-flow encodings (bid/ask, buy/sell, delta, imbalance) which must also stay distinguishable under the CVD-safe palettes required by US-SET-005.
- **Non-colour encoding**: where the ledger found a surface depending on hue alone, add the glyph/sign/pattern encoding US-SET-005 mandates ("side and direction remain distinguishable without colour through glyphs, signs or patterns everywhere").
- **Disabled-with-reason**: replace bare disabled controls on RBAC- or environment-gated actions with CMP-079 RbacGate's disabled-with-reason pattern.
- **Estimated chips**: ensure every heuristic output carries CMP-227 EstimatedBadge with its methodology InfoPanel link, per the trading-safety group of §12.
- **Hit targets**: bring sub-minimum targets to 24 px compact / 40–44 px comfortable, or log an essential-exception with its compensating control.
- **Storybook conformance**: add the missing stories so each component's story matrix matches its `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` Variants × States entry, each passing axe-core.
- **Near-duplicate consolidation**: where the ledger found a one-off component duplicating an existing `CMP-*`, replace the one-off; no new CMP ids are created.
- **Motion conformance** from E49-D04: hardcoded durations replaced with motion tokens, missing reduced-motion variants implemented, non-essential motion honouring `prefers-reduced-motion` OR-ed with the US-SET-007 preference, including WebGL-drawn motion which must read the resolved preference explicitly.
- Ledger rows updated to `pass` with evidence as each screen is remediated.

## Out of scope
- Redesign. Where the built screen differs from the spec and the *spec* is wrong, the discrepancy is escalated to design under `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §13.5 change control, not fixed by inventing a third option.
- Accessibility conformance findings owned by **E47**; this story fixes only design-system-class findings, though many overlap and the overlap is fixed once and recorded in both ledgers.
- Empty/loading/error state structure — E49-S05.
- Copy — E49-S06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hardcoded values cannot come back
  Given the token lint rule is enabled
  When a pull request introduces a raw hex colour or a raw px spacing value in a component style
  Then CI fails and names the file, line and the token that should be used
  And the rule has an allowlist only for the token definition files themselves

Scenario: A screen passes in every theme and density
  Given a remediated screen
  When it is verified across dark, light and high-contrast at compact and comfortable density
  Then no layout clipping, overlap or unreadable contrast occurs in any of the six combinations
  And the ledger row records evidence for all six

Scenario: Order-flow meaning survives colour blindness
  Given a CVD-safe palette is selected
  When any chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubble or profile surface is inspected
  Then buy versus sell and bid versus ask remain distinguishable without relying on hue
  And an automated check asserts no view depends on hue alone

Scenario: A disabled control explains itself
  Given a Manager views a control permitted only to the Owner
  When the control is rendered
  Then it uses the disabled-with-reason pattern naming the missing permission
  And a screen reader announces both the control name and the reason

Scenario: Reduced motion is honoured including on the canvas
  Given the operating system reports prefers-reduced-motion reduce
  When chart inertia, heatmap fades and panel transitions are exercised
  Then each reaches its final state within one frame or within the specified cross-fade budget
  And the WebGL-drawn motion is reduced as well as the DOM motion

Scenario: The spec itself is wrong
  Given a finding where the built behaviour is correct and the Figma spec is outdated
  When it is triaged
  Then it is escalated through design change control and the spec is updated
  And the ledger row is resolved as spec-corrected, not as a build fix
```

## Technical notes / design
- Work is batched by *finding class* (tokens, contrast, density, disabled-reason, chips, targets, stories, motion) rather than by screen, because a class fix is usually one change applied broadly and reviews far better than a per-screen shotgun.
- Token lint: `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` (or equivalent) for CSS and a custom ESLint rule for inline style objects and styled-component template literals; allowlist limited to the token source files.
- Hue-independence check: a build-time assertion over the theme definitions plus a Storybook visual test rendered through a CVD simulation matrix (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) asserting that paired semantic colours remain distinguishable by a measured perceptual distance, with the glyph/sign encoding present where the distance is insufficient.
- WebGL motion: the engine subscribes to the resolved reduced-motion preference (OS OR in-app, where in-app may only increase reduction) and switches interpolation off at the source rather than shortening durations, so no partial animation remains.
- Every remediated screen updates its ledger row in the same PR as the fix, so the ledger cannot drift from the code.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: lint rules tested against fixture violations and legal code; the hue-independence assertion tested against a deliberately hue-only palette (must fail) and a compliant one (must pass).
- **Storybook + axe**: every added story runs `vitest-axe`; the story-matrix conformance script from E49-D05 must pass for touched components.
- **Visual regression**: screenshot comparison per remediated component across the six theme × density combinations, with baselines committed.
- **E2E**: `@axe-core/playwright` on remediated screens in the existing suites; the motion spec `tests/e2e/motion-inventory.spec.ts` from E49-D04 must pass with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated.
- **Perf**: E46 budget checks required; visual tests run on the reference configuration and not in degraded rendering.
- **Coverage**: ≥80% frontend; no baseline regression.

## Security notes
Design remediation touches RBAC-gated controls and estimated-value disclosure, both of which have security-adjacent failure modes. The disabled-with-reason pattern must name the missing *permission*, not the existence of a resource the actor may not know about (the SCR-154 constraint); reviewers check each converted control for that. Estimated chips are an advice-boundary control: removing or weakening one would present a heuristic as fact, which `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` explicitly forbids for iceberg and stop-run detection. Data classification: no secrets touched; UI-only. No new attack surface introduced.

## Accessibility notes
This story carries substantial a11y content: contrast fixes, non-colour encoding, hit targets, focus visibility, disabled-with-reason announcements and reduced-motion. Each remediated screen must pass axe-core, be operable keyboard-only, and have correct focus order and visible focus per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Canvas-adjacent components must keep the DOM-mirror or non-spatial-alternative strategy specified in §6 — a token or layout change must not detach the mirror. Findings overlapping **E47** are fixed once and recorded in both ledgers to avoid double work and double counting.

## Performance notes
Token and style changes can silently add layout cost. E46's CI-enforced budgets are required checks; any remediated screen on a trading-critical path records a frame-budget check via the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay before and after. Storybook visual tests must not be run against a build in `degraded-2d`.

## Observability
No new runtime telemetry. Ledger counts flow to the burn-down dashboard's `design_qa_findings_open` series (E49-T02), which is how progress on this story is read.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ledger findings of design-system class resolved as fixed, spec-corrected or accepted-exception with owner and follow-up.
- [ ] Token lint rules enabled and CI-blocking.
- [ ] Six theme × density combinations verified per remediated screen with evidence in the ledger.
- [ ] Hue-independence check green; CVD simulation matrix passing.
- [ ] Storybook story matrix matches the component catalogue for touched components; all stories axe-clean.
- [ ] Reduced-motion behaviour verified including WebGL surfaces.
- [ ] Visual-regression baselines committed and green.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend; no baseline regression.
- [ ] perf: no E46 budget regression.
- [ ] design-qa: findings re-verified by a designer; ledger rows updated in the same PRs.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Demo at Sprint Review with before/after across themes.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E49-D01** supplies the ledger, severities and the calibrated effort model that sizes this story.
- **E49-D04** supplies the motion inventory and the reduced-motion mapping.
- **E47** overlaps on a11y-class findings; overlap is fixed once, recorded twice.

## Branch
`fix/e49-design-qa-<class>` per finding class · PR size ≤400 LOC; one finding class per PR.

## References
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §2 tokens, §7 motion, §12 design-QA checklist, §13.5 change control.
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-079 RbacGate, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, and the Variants × States matrices.

title: Bring every empty, loading and error surface into state-pattern conformance
body:
## Context
The nine shared state patterns in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-150 boot, SCR-151 empty, SCR-152 disconnected, SCR-153 degraded, SCR-154 403, SCR-155 404, SCR-156 crash boundary, SCR-157 version mismatch, SCR-158 rate-limited, SCR-159 offline/shell — were specified once and then instantiated independently by every epic that shipped a panel. R5 goal 3 includes an explicit empty/loading/error state audit. E49-D02 produced the normative spec and the conformance rubric; E49-Q04 produced the black-box state matrix that says which surface is currently wrong.

This story makes every surface conform. It matters beyond polish: several of these patterns carry safety and security requirements. SCR-152 must state that trading is disabled while offline *and* that exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected; SCR-153 must name precisely which capability is degraded and what still works; SCR-155 requires admin routes to 404 for non-owners with copy identical to any other 404 so the admin area's existence is not disclosed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Empty states (SCR-151)**: every panel that can be empty uses CMP-026 EmptyState with the mandated anatomy — heading stating the fact, one sentence of cause, one primary action, one secondary learn-more — in the correct one of three classes (nothing created yet / nothing matches the filter / data not recorded yet), with the role-aware action-vs-explanation variant, and the recorder-dependent variant carrying the recording-start timestamp. Catalogued instances to cover: empty workspace, no positions, no orders, no rules, no alerts, no journal trades, no watchlist symbols, no recorded history, no replay coverage, no audit results for a filter, no scanner matches, no notifications.
- **Loading states**: applied per E49-D02's decision table — CMP-015 Skeleton / CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart where layout is known, CMP-038 InlineSpinnerText for short inline waits, CMP-023 Progress Bar for determinate work. Bare spinners with no description are removed.
- **Boot (SCR-150)**: staged progress with named stages, per-stage timeout with an actionable failure, 5 s still-working message, 15 s cancel/reload, and the rule that DEMO/LIVE is not displayed until actually known.
- **Disconnected (SCR-152)**: global banner plus per-panel stale shading (CMP-076/077/078), last-good timestamp per affected panel, trading controls hard-disabled with the reason visible, the native-stops reassurance where true, and the post-reconnect divergence report ("While you were offline: 1 order filled, 1 stop moved by a rule").
- **Degraded (SCR-153)**: per-cause variants with CMP-092, disclosed feature-shedding, manual reduce-quality control, exit/restore state, and unambiguous statement of whether trading remains possible.
- **403 / 404 (SCR-154 / SCR-155)**: CMP-089 / CMP-090 with the disclosure constraints, correlation id as selectable text, request-access route, nearest-valid-destination links, and distinct deleted-object versus unknown-route copy.
- **Crash boundary (SCR-156)**: panel-level boundaries that keep the workspace alive — in particular never taking down the positions grid or the order ticket — plus route-level fallback, correlation id, copy-diagnostics, and a repeated-crash state that stops auto-remounting and explains why.
- **Version mismatch (SCR-157)**, **rate-limited (SCR-158)** and **offline/shell (SCR-159)** variants per their catalogue entries, including the held-action queue with explicit replay confirmation and the do-not-update-mid-trade guidance with the open-position count.
- **Analytics conformance**: each state emits the event and payload fixed by E49-D02 (`empty_state_shown{surface,reason}`, `error.403_shown`, `error.404_shown`, `app.error_boundary_triggered{component,correlationId,stackHash}`, `degraded.entered{cause,sheddedFeatures}`, `ratelimit.hit{scope,endpointClass,retryAfterMs}`).
- **A reusable state harness** so a panel declares its state contract once rather than hand-rolling each surface, preventing recurrence.

## Out of scope
- The wording itself — E49-S06 supplies final copy; this story installs the correct structure and slots.
- New state patterns; SCR-150…SCR-159 is a closed set.
- Changing the underlying failure behaviour (reconnect strategy, load shedding) — those are **E45** and **E46** concerns; this story surfaces them correctly.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No bare empty surface remains
  Given every panel enumerated in the SCR-151 catalogued instances
  When each is driven to its empty condition by the state-matrix harness
  Then it renders a heading, a causal sentence and either an action or an explicit statement that no action is available to this role
  And no surface renders a bare "No data" string or an icon alone

Scenario: A crashing panel does not take the workspace down
  Given the order ticket panel and the positions grid are mounted
  When an unrelated panel throws during render
  Then only that panel is replaced by the panel-level boundary
  And the positions grid and order ticket remain mounted and interactive
  And the boundary shows a correlation id and a copy-diagnostics action

Scenario: Offline trading block is explicit and reassuring
  Given the private websocket disconnects
  When the disconnected state renders
  Then order entry controls are disabled with the reason stated
  And each affected panel shows its last-good timestamp
  And the statement that exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected is shown where true

Scenario: Admin routes do not disclose themselves
  Given a Viewer navigates to an admin-only route
  When the response renders
  Then a 404 is shown with copy identical to any other unknown-route 404
  And no text or network response distinguishes it from a route that does not exist

Scenario: Empty surfaces are free
  Given a panel in its empty state
  When resource usage is measured
  Then no WebGL context is created and no market-data subscription is opened for that panel

Scenario: Repeated crashes stop the loop
  Given a panel crashes three times within one minute
  When the boundary re-evaluates
  Then it stops auto-remounting, explains why, and offers remove-panel and reload-app actions
```

## Technical notes / design
- **State harness**: a small `PanelState` contract (`idle | loading | empty | error | stale | degraded | forbidden | notFound`) that a panel returns; a shared renderer maps each to the correct component recipe from E49-D02. Panels stop hand-rolling states, which is what makes the fix durable rather than a one-time cleanup.
- Empty-state laziness is enforced structurally: the harness renders the empty branch *before* any data-dependent child mounts, so no GL context or subscription is created (the SCR-151 performance clause).
- Error boundaries are installed per panel at the docking-layout level and per route at the router level; the repeated-crash policy uses a rolling window keyed by panel id and stack hash.
- 403/404 parity is enforced at the API layer as well as the UI: the server returns 404 for admin resources to unauthorised actors so the UI cannot leak by rendering a different state; the response body shape is identical.
- Correlation ids are opaque, generated server-side, and selectable text in the UI (screen-reader friendly and copyable).
- Held-action queue for SCR-158 stores the user's intent and requires explicit confirmation to replay — never silent replay of an order after a rate-limit window.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: the state harness mapping for all eight states; the repeated-crash rolling-window policy; the held-action queue's explicit-confirmation requirement; the empty-branch laziness assertion (no GL context, no subscription).
- **Integration**: forced 403/404 responses; forced degraded causes; forced rate-limit `10018`; server-side parity test asserting identical bodies for admin-404 versus unknown-route-404.
- **E2E**: the state matrix from E49-Q04 driven through Playwright for web and Electron — every panel × every applicable state, asserting structure and accessible semantics, not pixels.
- **Chaos**: WS disconnect storm and reconnect, backend 5xx, Postgres unavailability and Electron renderer crash mid-order from `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §9, asserting the correct state surfaces and that trading is blocked where required.
- **A11y**: axe-core on every state; manual screen-reader spot-check of SCR-152's alert-then-banner behaviour and SCR-153's status announcement.
- **Perf**: empty-panel resource assertion; SCR-154's ≤200 ms render; SCR-150's ≤2.5 s cold start to interactive shell.
- **Coverage**: ≥80% frontend, ≥85% for any backend parity code.

## Security notes
This story implements two explicit information-disclosure controls from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and the catalogue: (1) admin routes 404 identically to unknown routes for non-owners, enforced at both API and UI layers and tested for body parity; (2) the 403 names the missing permission without revealing whether an admin-only resource exists. Additionally: correlation ids must not encode user or account identifiers; the crash boundary's diagnostics bundle must be scrubbed of API keys, session tokens and account balances before it is copyable; the held-action replay queue must re-authorise on replay rather than reusing a stale authorisation decision. Reviewed by the Security engineer; abuse cases are covered in E49-X01.

## Accessibility notes
Normative per the catalogue: SCR-150 announces progress politely per phase and never shows a bare spinner; SCR-151 always has a heading plus causal sentence plus an action or an explicit no-action statement; SCR-152 fires `role="alert"` once then persists as a banner and does not announce the countdown every tick; SCR-153 uses `role="status"` naming the degraded capability, with per-panel badges repeating it in their accessible name; SCR-154's correlation id is selectable text; SCR-156 uses a `role="alert"` region with the stack trace behind a control labelled as technical detail; SCR-158 announces countdowns at most once per 10 s. Each is asserted in the E2E state matrix.

## Performance notes
Budgets restated from the catalogue and enforced: empty surfaces initialise no heavy resources; SCR-154 renders in ≤200 ms from the server's 403 with no extra fetches; SCR-155 resolves client-side with no network call; SCR-150 reaches an interactive shell in ≤2.5 s on the reference machine; SCR-152 reaches time-to-usable ≤5 s after a 30 s outage with subscriptions restored in priority order (private account state, focused panel, then the rest). ## Context
E49-D03 produced the terminology lexicon, the voice and error-message standards, the safety-copy and estimated-disclosure rules, and a graded string inventory with proposed rewrites. This story applies them. The roadmap lists a copy review as explicit E49 scope (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2).

Copy here is functional, not decorative. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` makes specific sentences mandatory (SCR-152's trading-disabled and stop-loss-unaffected statements; SCR-154's named permission and "ask the owner" guidance), and `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` requires heuristic detector outputs to be presented as *estimated* rather than asserted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Apply the inventory's accepted rewrites** across components, screens, toasts, dialogs, tooltips, empty/error states and accessible names (`aria-label`, `title`, live-region text).
- **Terminology normalisation** to the lexicon's approved terms, removing banned synonyms — trade group, fan-out, native stop-loss, Demo/Live, arm/disarm, kill-switch, flatten, reduce-only, estimated, recorded history, replay, workspace, rule, alert, Owner/Manager/Viewer.
- **Error-registry copy**: every user-facing REST/WS error message (registry referenced by `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`) states what happened, why and what to do next, with a correlation id available and the code never shown alone.
- **Safety copy**: destructive and trading confirms (US-SET-003 surfaces SCR-015, SCR-029, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-129) name the exact quantity, symbol, account count and environment; hold-to-confirm states its duration; the Live variant is never softer than the Demo variant.
- **Estimated disclosure**: every heuristic output uses "estimated", carries CMP-227 and links its methodology InfoPanel; "detected", "confirmed" and "signal" are removed for heuristic outputs.
- **Time and number conformance** per US-SET-006: display honours the user's zone and separators with the zone labelled wherever a timestamp appears; every export is ISO-8601 with an explicit offset regardless of display settings; a single shared formatting utility is used everywhere.
- **Banned-synonym lint rule** implemented from E49-D03's specification, fed by the lexicon file, CI-blocking, with an allowlist for quoted exchange terminology.
- **Frozen-string protection**: safety-critical strings marked `frozen` in the lexicon are covered by a test asserting their exact text, so a future drive-by edit fails CI rather than silently weakening a warning.

## Out of scope
- Localisation or an i18n runtime.
- Changing behaviour to match copy: if copy is right and behaviour is wrong, a bug is filed against the owning area rather than the sentence being softened to match the bug.
- Documentation and user-guide prose — **E48**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Banned synonyms cannot return
  Given the banned-synonym lint rule is enabled
  When a pull request introduces the word "basket" for a trade group in user-visible text
  Then CI fails naming the file, the banned term and the approved replacement
  And quoted exchange terminology on the allowlist does not trigger the rule

Scenario: Every error message is actionable
  Given any user-facing error surfaced from the error registry
  When it is displayed
  Then it states what happened, why, and what to do next, and a correlation id is available
  And the bare error code is never the entire message

Scenario: A destructive confirm states the real consequence
  Given a flatten-all action in Live across three accounts
  When the confirm is shown
  Then it names the environment, the account count, the affected symbols and the total quantity
  And the hold-to-confirm duration is stated and visibly indicated

Scenario: Heuristics are not asserted as fact
  Given an iceberg or stop-run detector output
  When its label is rendered
  Then it reads as estimated, carries the estimated badge and links to its methodology
  And the words detected or confirmed do not appear for that output

Scenario: Exports are unambiguous regardless of display settings
  Given a user has selected local time and comma thousands separators
  When any CSV or JSON export is produced
  Then every timestamp is ISO-8601 with an explicit offset and numbers are locale-independent

Scenario: A frozen string is protected
  Given a safety-critical string marked frozen in the lexicon
  When a pull request changes its text
  Then the frozen-string test fails and the change requires design and security review to proceed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Application is mechanical and reviewable: the inventory CSV drives a checklist; each PR covers one surface family (order ticket, positions, admin, alerts, replay, rules, settings, states) so reviewers can read it as prose.
- Accessible names are treated as first-class strings: an `aria-label` change is reviewed for whether it still makes sense out of context.
- Time/number formatting is consolidated into one utility; per-surface ad-hoc formatting is deleted, which is what makes US-SET-006's "one formatting utility used everywhere" true rather than aspirational.
- Frozen strings are asserted by exact-match tests with the lexicon as the source of truth; the test names the review requirement in its failure message so the next engineer knows what to do.
- Analytics enums that embed copy-like values (`empty_state_shown{reason}`, `degraded.entered{cause}`) are *not* renamed by this story unless E49-D03 listed them, since renaming silently breaks dashboards; any necessary rename is coordinated with the dashboard owner.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: the banned-synonym rule against fixture sources (violation, allowlisted quote, code identifier that merely contains the term); frozen-string exact-match tests; the formatting utility across zones, DST boundaries, negative numbers, large quantities and precision edge cases.
- **Integration**: error-registry rendering test asserting every registry entry produces a complete user-facing message.
- **E2E**: confirm-dialog content assertions for flatten, cancel-all, reverse and freeze in both Demo and Live variants, asserting Live is never softer.
- **A11y**: axe-core on touched screens; screen-reader spot-check that renamed accessible names still identify their controls unambiguously.
- **Export tests**: ISO-8601-with-offset assertion across every export path (journal, audit, positions, orders).
- **Coverage**: ≥80% frontend; ≥85% for the shared formatting utility if it lives in a shared package.

## Security notes
Copy changes are a live information-disclosure surface. Enforced here: no raw exception text, stack fragments, internal hostnames, file paths, account identifiers or key fragments in user-facing strings (SCR-156 keeps technical detail behind a disclosure control); 403/404 wording preserves the non-disclosure of admin-only resources (SCR-154, SCR-155); correlation ids remain opaque. A "clarifying" rewrite of an authorisation error is a classic accidental leak, so every touched auth or admin string gets Security-engineer review. Frozen-string protection is itself a security control: it prevents a future edit from weakening a Live-environment warning.

## Accessibility notes
Per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: accessible names must make sense out of context; no reliance on visual position; live-region text must stay short enough to be useful at the user's configured verbosity (US-SET-007 verbosity levels); colour words must not be the sole carrier of meaning ("buy side", not "the green side"); error text must be associated with its control programmatically, not merely placed nearby.

## Performance notes
N/A at runtime beyond the formatting-utility consolidation, which removes duplicated per-surface formatting work on hot paths (positions grid, DOM ladder, footprint tooltips). Where consolidation touches a high-frequency render path, a before/after frame-budget measurement is recorded and E46's budget checks must stay green.

Analytics enum values containing copy-like reasons are preserved unless explicitly listed for rename by E49-D03; any rename is coordinated with the dashboard owner and the affected Grafana queries are updated in the same change.

- [ ] All accepted inventory rewrites applied; inventory verdicts updated to done.
- [ ] Terminology normalised; banned-synonym lint rule CI-blocking.
- [ ] Error-registry messages complete; correlation ids available.
- [ ] Safety copy verified across all destructive-action surfaces in both environments.

- [ ] security: Security-engineer review of auth, admin and error copy.
- [ ] design-qa: copy compared against the spec by a designer; ledger updated.

title: Resolve hotkey conflicts and make invalid-context bindings explain themselves
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 lists a **hotkey conflict audit** as E49 scope. E49-T04 built the oracle: a single keymap source of truth plus a CI lint for same-context collisions, undeclared global shadowing, reserved-key clashes, destructive-binding safety and catalogue drift. This story fixes everything that lint reports and closes the behavioural gaps in US-SET-002's three Must scenarios.

The third scenario in particular is usually unimplemented in practice: *"it works in every view where flattening is valid, and is inert elsewhere with an explanation on press"*. A silently-inert hotkey is indistinguishable from a broken app, and in a trading context a user who believes they pressed flatten and received no feedback is in a genuinely dangerous state.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Resolve every conflict** reported by the E49-T04 lint: same-context collisions re-bound with the Owner's input on which command keeps the key; undeclared cross-context shadows either declared with a rationale or re-bound; reserved-key clashes removed or converted into reviewed, documented overrides.
- **Inert-with-explanation**: pressing a valid-but-not-here command shows a brief, non-modal explanation naming the command and why it is not available in this context ("Flatten all is not available while the rule editor has focus"), using the existing toast host SCR-015 / CMP-045 with a rate limit so repeated presses do not spam.
- **Destructive-command safety defaults**: flatten, cancel-all, freeze and kill-switch require a modifier by default per SCR-113's safety group; any that do not are re-bound; the setting remains user-changeable with the change audited as `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`.
- **Conflict UI conformance** (SCR-113): saving a colliding binding is blocked with both commands named and the context stated; reserved keys are refused with the reason; the keyboard-only alternative to key capture (modifier and key selects) works.
- **Cheatsheet conformance** (SCR-013): the overlay renders the user's *current* bindings grouped by context as a real table for screen readers, highlights conflicts with a warning chip, and links to SCR-113.
- **Import/export safety**: an imported keymap profile is validated against the same conflict and reserved-key rules before it is applied, with a per-binding report of what was rejected and why — an import must never silently install a conflicting or unsafe binding.
- **Regression guards**: E2E tests per resolved conflict class so the fix is protected beyond the build-time lint.

## Out of scope
- Adding commands or redesigning the keymap philosophy; one global layer with context scoping is the locked design from US-SET-002.
- Per-view hotkey schemes — explicitly forbidden by the story's NFR ("one hotkey layer, not per-view schemes").
- Changing the hotkey editor's visual design; only behavioural conformance is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The lint is clean
  Given the keymap after remediation
  When the E49-T04 lint runs in CI
  Then it reports zero same-context collisions, zero undeclared global shadows and zero unjustified reserved-key clashes

Scenario: An inert press explains itself
  Given the rule editor has focus and the user presses the flatten-all binding
  When the command is evaluated
  Then a brief explanation names the command and states why it is unavailable here
  And nothing is flattened
  And repeated presses within five seconds do not produce repeated notifications

Scenario: A conflicting rebind is refused
  Given Escape is already bound to Close dialog in the Global context
  When the user tries to bind Escape to Cancel all orders in the Global context
  Then saving is blocked, both commands are named, and the user is offered reassign or choose-another

Scenario: A reserved key is refused with the reason
  Given the user attempts to bind Ctrl+Shift+I
  When the binding is captured
  Then it is refused and the reason names the reserving platform

Scenario: Destructive commands need a modifier by default
  Given a fresh profile with default settings
  When the bindings for flatten, cancel-all, freeze and kill-switch are inspected
  Then each requires at least one modifier
  And changing one to a bare key requires acknowledging a warning and is audited

Scenario: An unsafe import is rejected per binding
  Given an exported keymap containing a same-context collision and a reserved key
  When it is imported
  Then the safe bindings are applied and the unsafe ones are listed with reasons
  And no conflicting binding is silently installed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Command dispatch goes through the E49-T04 dispatcher: resolve binding → command id → evaluate `validWhen` for the current context → execute, or emit the inert explanation. This puts the "explain on press" behaviour in one place instead of per view.
- Rate limiting for inert explanations: at most one notification per command per 5 s, keyed by command id, so holding a key does not flood SCR-015.
- Re-binding decisions that affect muscle memory are made with the Owner (who is the primary user) rather than by engineering preference; each decision is recorded in the keymap entry's comment so its rationale survives.
- Import validation reuses the lint's rule implementations so the build-time and runtime rules cannot diverge — a single module used by both.
- Audit emission for trading-binding changes uses CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger so the audit cannot be bypassed by a code path that forgets to emit.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: dispatcher context evaluation for each command's `validWhen`; inert-explanation rate limiter; import validator against fixture profiles (clean, colliding, reserved, unknown command id, version mismatch).
- **Integration**: rebinding via SCR-113 persists and takes effect without reload (per SCR-113's performance note).
- **E2E (web + Electron)**: one scenario per resolved conflict class; the inert-explanation scenario; the refused-rebind scenario; the reserved-key scenario; the destructive-default scenario; the import-rejection scenario. Electron matters here because shell-reserved keys differ from browser-reserved keys.
- **A11y**: the cheatsheet renders as a real table; key capture has a working keyboard-only alternative; the inert explanation is announced politely without stealing focus.
- **Perf**: conflict detection stays an O(1) map lookup; no measurable added input latency — verified against E46's input-stage budget.
- **Coverage**: ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
Hotkeys can fire irreversible trading actions. Controls preserved and tested here: destructive commands require a modifier by default; changing a trading binding is audited as `hotkey.trading_binding_changed` because it alters the risk surface of muscle memory; an imported profile is validated before application so a shared or tampered profile cannot bind flatten to a bare key; the confirm policy from US-SET-003 still applies on execution, so a hotkey never bypasses a required confirm — a hotkey that reached a destructive action without the configured confirm would be a P0. Security-engineer review is required on the dispatcher's destructive path and the import validator.

## Accessibility notes
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires full keyboard operability, which this story protects rather than threatens — but the inert-explanation notification must be announced politely (`role="status"`) without stealing focus, and must not fire so often that it makes the app unusable with a screen reader. SCR-013's cheatsheet must be a real table with a printable stylesheet. SCR-113's key capture must retain its keyboard-only alternative. Any command reachable only by hotkey is given a visible control or an explicit exception with rationale, per E49-T04's check.

## Performance notes
SCR-113: binding capture is local and conflict detection is an O(1) lookup against the binding map; saving applies immediately without reload. SCR-013: the overlay mounts in ≤80 ms and must not pause the chart render loop. The dispatcher sits on the input path, so E46's input-stage budget is a required check — an added context evaluation must not measurably increase input-to-action latency.

## Observability
`hotkey.changed{action, before, after}`, `hotkey.reset` and `hotkey.profile_imported` remain analytics events; `hotkey.trading_binding_changed` remains an audit record. New: a counter for inert-press explanations by command id, which reveals commands users expect to work in contexts where they do not — a product signal, not just a defect signal.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Keymap lint clean; every conflict resolved with a recorded rationale.
- [ ] Inert-with-explanation implemented, rate-limited and announced accessibly.
- [ ] Destructive-command modifier defaults in place; changes audited.
- [ ] SCR-113 conflict refusal, reserved-key refusal and keyboard-only capture verified.
- [ ] SCR-013 cheatsheet renders current bindings with conflict chips.
- [ ] Import validation rejects unsafe bindings per binding with reasons.
- [ ] E2E guards per conflict class green on web and Electron.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green; polite announcement verified with a screen reader.
- [ ] perf: no input-latency regression against E46's budget.
- [ ] security: Security-engineer review of the destructive path and import validator.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Docs: default keymap table regenerated for E48's user guide.
- [ ] Demo at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

- **E48** consumes the regenerated keymap table for the user guide.

## Branch
